options: than it was a few days before
explanation: 'More warmer' is a double comparative since 'warmer' is already comparative; correct it to 'much warmer'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Shivam is much cleverer than any other boy in the office.
explanation: No error: 'much cleverer' is a valid intensified comparative and 'than any other boy' is the correct structure for comparing one member with the rest of the group.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: His struggles were becoming more and more frenzier, / a wild look creeping into his blue eyes.
options: a wild look creeping into his blue eyes.
explanation: 'Frenzier' is not a valid comparative form; the adjective is 'frenzied', so it should be 'more and more frenzied'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The construction of / the new business school / is led to / a sudden rise of population in our area.
options: a sudden rise of population in our area
explanation: The construction actively caused the rise, so the passive 'is led to' is wrong; use the present perfect active 'has led to'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: What would / happen if / human beings were / governing by robots?
explanation: After 'were', the passive requires the past participle, so 'governing by robots' must become 'governed by robots'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: My friends are gone on a trip to Goa today.
explanation: 'Are gone' wrongly uses 'be' with an intransitive verb of movement; the present perfect 'have gone' is required.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: One of the students is always / late to the class; he has warned / by the teacher many times; / but still, he keeps on being late.
options: One of the students is always
but still, he keeps on being late
late to the class; he has warned
explanation: The student receives the warning, so the passive is needed: 'he has been warned by the teacher', not 'he has warned'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The man who / was committed / the theft last night / was caught this evening.
explanation: The man performed the theft, so the active past tense 'committed' is required instead of the passive 'was committed'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: He was unable / to help me because / he had been failed / to arrange the money.
explanation: 'Fail' is intransitive and cannot be passive here; it should be 'he had failed to arrange the money'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Electric heaters were providing to all the officers at the guest house.
explanation: The heaters received the action, so the passive past participle is needed: 'were provided to all the officers'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I think someone has been picked my pocket while I was travelling in the metro.
options: someone has been picked my pocket
explanation: 'Has been picked' is passive yet takes the object 'my pocket'; the active 'someone has picked my pocket' is correct.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Bags and purses were thoroughly checking at the entrance to the theatre.
explanation: Bags and purses are the receivers of the checking, so the passive 'were thoroughly checked' is required, not the continuous active form.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The children were warning / not to try / to climb the cliffs / as they were very steep.
explanation: The children received the warning, so the passive 'were warned' must replace the active 'were warning'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: My tailor is made / some very stylish dresses / for me as well as / for my daughter.
explanation: The tailor performs the action, so 'is made' should be the active present perfect 'has made'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Despite warnings / the driver continued to speed / and has caught / by the traffic police.
explanation: The driver was the one caught, so the passive past tense 'was caught' is needed instead of the active 'has caught'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: She managed the company / so well that it is made / a huge profit that year.
options: so well that it is made
explanation: The company earned the profit, so the past active 'it made a huge profit' replaces the passive present 'it is made'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Smart phone age has been led / to substantial deterioration in / both duration and quality of sleep.
options: Smart phone age has been led
both duration and quality of sleep.
explanation: 'Lead to' is active here, so the passive 'has been led' is wrong; it should be 'Smart phone age has led to'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Personal care products can / make from agricultural ingredients, / such as flower or fruit extracts and oils.
options: such as flower or fruit extracts and oils.
explanation: The products are the receivers of the making, so after 'can' the passive infinitive is needed: 'can be made from agricultural ingredients'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Antonio Stradivari was an Italian who is being made wonderful violins.
explanation: The sentence states a past fact about Stradivari's completed work, so the present continuous passive 'is being made' is wrong; it must be the simple past active 'who made wonderful violins'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Why should I be suspect by you?
explanation: A passive construction needs the past participle, not the base form: 'be suspect' must become 'be suspected' — 'Why should I be suspected by you?'

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: We have been / arranged the stay / for the guests at / a hillside resort.
explanation: 'We' is the doer of the arranging, so the passive 'have been arranged' is wrong; 'We have been' should be 'We have' to give the active present perfect 'We have arranged the stay'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: We will / have been known the result / of the CAT exam by next week.
options: of the CAT exam by next week
explanation: 'Know' here is active (we do the knowing), so 'will have been known the result' is faulty; it should be the future perfect active 'will have known the result'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: He had been improving / his communication skills in order / to shine in his career.
explanation: No error — 'had been improving' (past perfect continuous) correctly shows an ongoing past effort, and 'in order to shine' is the proper infinitive of purpose.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Are you sure that / you will be broadcasted / the news to everyone / across the country?

sentence: The school authorities are / decided to close the high school / wing for the next three days / due to power failure.

wing for the next three days

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: One-to-one interaction / with parents is knowing / to be important.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The government has been / accused of not doing enough / to combat climate change.

sentence: The gentleman (1) / together with his (2) / wife and daughter were drowned. (3) / No Error (4)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').

sentence: Mr. Malhotra, including (a) / his friends, were (b) / invited to dinner, (c) / No error (d)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The teacher as well as the students (a) / have gone on an excursion (b) / to Ooty during the summer vacation, (c) / No error (d)

to Ooty during the summer vacation,

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Vijay unlike his friends (a) / are not going to miss (b) / the class tomorrow, (c) / No error (d)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Patience as well as perseverance (a) / are necessary (b) / for success, (c) / No error (d)

sentence: The players except the captain (a) / are practising very hard (b) / for the forthcoming match, (c) / No error (d)

sentence: The journalist besides (1) / the camera crew were (2) / kidnapped by the militants last night. (3) / No error (4)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').

sentence: The rural poor (1) / can neither migrate to (2) / the urban areas or afford the very high fees charged by the corporate private schools (3) / No Error (4)

sentence: Neither the famine (a)/ or the subsequent fire (b)/ was able to destroy the spirit of the people (c)/ No error (d)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Neither of the contestant was (a)/ in a proper physical condition (b)/ to do his best work (c)/ No Error (d)
explanation: 'Neither of' is followed by a plural noun since it refers to two people. Change 'Neither of the contestant was' to 'Neither of the contestants was'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I am certain that none (a)/ of these two books is useful to the (b)/ students of the 8th standard (c)/ No Error (d)
options: of these two books is useful to the
explanation: 'None' is used for more than two; for exactly two ('these two books') 'neither' is required. Change 'none' to 'neither'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Neither Raju is intelligent (A)/ nor hardworking (B)/ and still he expects (C)/ a handsome salary. (D)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Neither he nor they (a)/ is making any strategy (b)/ for the company, (c)/ No error, (d)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Not only Sanya (1)/ and also Sam (2)/ has failed the examination (3)/ No error (4)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Neither the reporters nor the editor (A)/ were satisfied by the attitude (B)/ of the publishers of the newspaper. (C)/ No error (D)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Either sohan or his friends (a)/ is to be blamed (b)/ for this mischief, (c)/ No error (d)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Either parmeet (a)/ or jyoti (b)/ have committed the crime, (c)/ No error, (d)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: He'd no sooner (a)/ seen one continent (b)/ when he saw another (c)/ no error (d)

sentence: Hardly he had arrived (a)/ when the house caught fire (b)/ and everything was reduced to ashes (c)/ No Error (d)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Hardly we had reached (a)/ the platform (b)/ when the train started, (c)/ no error (d)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: No sooner did Priya / get her report card / when she started jumping / with joy.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Raman putted the vegetables / in the frying pan / and after adding some water, / closed the lid.

sentence: Though he had (a)/ a few doubts, (b)/ he didn't rise any question, (c)/ No error (d)

explanation: The future perfect is 'will have graduated'; 'will had graduated' is an incorrect verb form.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: People admired him, for / he lived by the same principals / that he preached.
options: he lived by the same principals
explanation: 'Principals' (heads of institutions) should be 'principles', meaning moral rules or beliefs.

prompt: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. Identify the part that has an error. Select 'No error' if there is no error.
sentence: Although the team had trained diligently for months, they had still overwhelmed by the opponent's unexpected tactics.
explanation: The team received the action, so the passive 'were still overwhelmed' is required instead of the active perfect 'had still overwhelmed'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: After the concert was over, / they go to a restaurant, / had dinner together / and talked until midnight.
explanation: The other verbs ('had', 'talked') are past, so the present 'go' must be 'went' for tense consistency.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My sister and I / work very hard / nevertheless my brother does not do / any task assigned to him.
options: nevertheless my brother does not do
explanation: 'Nevertheless' is a conjunctive adverb and cannot join the clauses here; a contrast conjunction like 'but' or 'whereas' is needed.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Having known that / the train was already on the platform, / they ran fastly / to catch it.
options: the train was already on the platform
explanation: 'Fastly' is not a word; 'fast' serves as both adjective and adverb, so it should be 'ran fast'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in the usage of the interjection.
sentence: He replied / in a dry tone, / “Ouch! I will not work / for you anymore.”
explanation: 'Ouch!' expresses sudden pain and does not suit a dry, refusing tone; an interjection like 'Well!' or 'Alas!' would fit.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Every students in the hostel decided to travel to Delhi to witness the Republic Day parade.
explanation: 'Every' is always followed by a singular noun, so it must be 'Every student in the hostel'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. We took dinner in a Chinese restaurant and were amazed to see the interior of a restaurant.
explanation: The restaurant has already been specified, so the definite article is required: 'the interior of the restaurant'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The lions became violently / when the visitors / started throwing / stones at them.
explanation: After the linking verb 'became' an adjective is needed, so 'violently' must be 'violent'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Please go and meet the chairperson. / She will be / away for the / few next days.
options: Please go and meet the chairperson.
explanation: The correct order places the ordinal-type word first: 'the next few days', not 'the few next days'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. He always wants to be in the company of those who are intellectually superior than him.
explanation: Latin comparatives ending in '-ior' such as 'superior' take 'to', so it should be 'superior to him'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Mr. Abhilash and his family / have received / no informations / about the incident.
explanation: 'Information' is an uncountable noun and has no plural form, so 'no informations' should be 'no information'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My brother performed / extremely good / in the class test / held yesterday.
explanation: The action verb 'performed' needs the adverb 'well', not the adjective 'good' — 'performed extremely well'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The teacher asked him not to keep disturbing the class, but it had no affect.
explanation: The noun meaning 'result' is 'effect'; 'affect' is a verb, so it should be 'no effect'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Dr. Sinha has / brought about a new / book on social / impact of child labour.
explanation: 'Brought about' means 'caused'; for publishing a book the correct phrasal verb is 'brought out'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Mrs. Sreelakshmi’s / musical intelligence / is superior than / Mrs. Suma’s.
explanation: Adjectives ending in '-ior' like 'superior' are followed by 'to', never 'than'; correct form is 'is superior to'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: By the end of / this month, he / will been working / for five years.
explanation: 'will been working' is an incomplete verb form; the future perfect continuous requires 'will have been working'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. While I was walking to the store, my friend calls me and ask for a favour.
options: my friend calls me and ask
explanation: The past continuous 'was walking' fixes the sentence in the past, so the verbs must be 'called me and asked'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Solutions to the country’s interior problems are still a long way away.
explanation: 'Interior' refers to physical inside space; for a country's own affairs the correct adjective is 'internal problems'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The police told the agitators to back in, else they would lathi-charge.
explanation: 'back in' is the wrong phrasal verb here; the police would tell agitators 'to back off/back out'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: The principal gave up / the prizes to / the winners on / Republic Day.
explanation: 'gave up' means to surrender or quit; distributing prizes requires 'gave away' (or simply 'gave').

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He and his friends / does not / want to / attend the meeting.
explanation: The compound subject 'He and his friends' is plural, so the auxiliary must be 'do not', not 'does not'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The windows / violent banged / during the / storm yesterday.
explanation: The verb 'banged' needs an adverb, so 'violent' must become 'violently'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The tea at this café is best than at the Costa Café in our office.
explanation: A comparison between two things with 'than' takes the comparative degree: 'is better than', not the superlative 'best'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Mr. Surya / have no interior / motive in offering / you support.
explanation: The singular proper-noun subject 'Mr. Surya' needs 'has', and the correct word is 'ulterior motive', not 'interior'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. No other place in this country is so better as Gulmarg, Kashmir.
explanation: The 'so...as' structure takes the positive degree, so it should be 'so good as', not the comparative 'better'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Deepak is studying B.tech. at IIT Delhi to become the engineer.
explanation: A profession mentioned generally takes the indefinite article: 'to become an engineer', not 'the engineer'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I have the hundred reasons to not attend the meeting tomorrow.
explanation: Numbers like hundred take 'a' in such expressions: 'a hundred reasons', not 'the hundred reasons'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. In some countries, you are not able to drink until you are 21.
explanation: The sentence is about legal permission, not physical ability, so 'able to drink' must be 'allowed to drink'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I have sing ‘Let It Go’ before a crowd of thousands of people.
explanation: After 'have' the third form of the verb is required: 'I have sung', not 'I have sing'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He never talks / for anybody. / He is alone / all day.
explanation: 'Talk' collocates with 'to' when addressing someone, so 'talks to anybody' is correct.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The supermarket is open from 10 a.m. still 10 p.m.
explanation: The time range needs the preposition 'till/to', so 'still 10 p.m.' should be 'till 10 p.m.'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My sister, Juliet, / got married / as her / was 23.
explanation: A clause subject needs the nominative pronoun and a time conjunction: 'when she was 23', not 'as her was 23'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Rahul thinks he is as smarter as his friends in the class.
explanation: The 'as...as' construction takes the positive degree, so it must be 'as smart as', not 'as smarter as'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. It is he who work for the company for more than a decade.
explanation: 'for more than a decade' signals present perfect and the verb must agree with 'he', so 'who has worked' is correct.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I are dancing with my husband at my sister’s wedding.
explanation: The pronoun 'I' takes 'am', not 'are'; the correct form is 'I am dancing'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My dog / barks / very louder / at night.
explanation: 'Very' cannot modify a comparative, and the verb 'barks' needs an adverb: 'very loudly' (or 'much louder').

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Mr. Suman / asked me / to pack / my luggages.
explanation: 'Luggage' is an uncountable noun and has no plural form, so it should be 'my luggage'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: They secret / decided / to leave / the town.
explanation: The verb 'decided' needs the adverb 'secretly', not the adjective 'secret': 'They secretly decided'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. It rain a lot in this part of the country.
explanation: With the third-person singular subject 'It' in the simple present, the verb must be 'rains'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: He was / bad injured / in the / last match.
explanation: The past participle 'injured' must be modified by the adverb 'badly', not the adjective 'bad'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: It was not only the scattering of administrative authority across multiple agencies (1)/ that weakened coordinated policy-making, but the rigidity built into intersecting compliance frameworks (2)/ which, though intended to preserve procedural independence, (3)/ end up stalling inter-departmental coordination completely. (4)
explanation: The correlative 'not only' must be completed by 'but also', so segment 2 should read 'but also the rigidity'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The assumption, not that the reforms themselves were poorly designed but rather that their public messaging—filled with concepts distant from local conversations— (1)/ have led more to voter indifference (2)/ than administrative lapses as such, points to a wider institutional disconnect (3)/ than earlier admitted. (4)
explanation: The subject is the singular 'The assumption', so the verb should be 'has led', not 'have led'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: What makes the draft legislation especially contentious is not its proposed restructuring of fiscal authority per se, (1)/ but that it assumes, without empirical evidence, (2)/ a fiscal parity among states whose developmental starting points are (3)/ incomparable by any accepted standard. (4)
explanation: 'not ... but' must join parallel structures; the noun phrase in (1) is paired with a 'that' clause, so (2) should read 'but its assumption, without empirical evidence, of'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: That several civic bodies have revived obsolete regulations (1)/ to curb public criticism does not only indicate administrative expediency (2)/ but also weakens the democratic spirit (3)/ that those provisions were intended to safeguard. (4)
explanation: The correlative is 'not only ... but also' placed before parallel verbs: 'not only indicates ... but also weakens', not 'does not only indicate'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The committee’s recommendations, striking in both breadth and detail, (1)/ triggered reactions not only from the departments involved (2)/ but also from the reviewers who state they (3)/ had not been permitted to examine key files. (4)
explanation: The main verb 'triggered' is past, so the reporting verb must also be past: 'who stated they'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: That the policy omits provisions for backward compatibility (1) / is less troubling than the belief (2) / that all regional bodies will, without any pressure, (3) / complies with the central directive as issued (4).
explanation: After the modal 'will', the bare infinitive is required: 'comply', not 'complies'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Neither did the committee acknowledge the financial irregularities, (1)/ nor did they consider the repeated warnings (2)/ issued by auditors, which, according to reports, (3)/ has been ignored for a long time. (4)/
explanation: 'Which' refers to the plural 'warnings' in a past context, so it should be 'had been ignored', not 'has been ignored'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: What the organization did not examine thoroughly enough (1)/ were not the scheme’s objectives themselves, (2)/ but the political consequences it (3)/ might have caused if carried out without wider agreement. (4)
explanation: A 'what' clause as subject takes a singular verb, so it should be 'was not the scheme's objectives'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The report’s focus on tech-utopianism, though praiseworthy, (1)/ ignore the deep-rooted inequities (2)/ that continue in data availability and digital competence (3)/ across demographic and regional gaps. (4)
explanation: The subject is the singular 'The report's focus', so the verb must be 'ignores'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Neither the analysis of revenue nor the forecast of expenditure patterns (1)/ seem to reflect the supply bottlenecks (2)/ that medium-sized manufacturers experience (3)/ during sudden market contractions. (4)
explanation: With 'neither ... nor' joining two singular subjects, the verb agrees with the nearer singular noun: 'seems'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The claim that critical voices are suppressed (1) / in the absence of firm procedural checks (2) / indicate a disturbing
sentence: pattern of democratic decline (3) / visible at several layers of administration. (4)
explanation: The subject is the singular 'The claim', so the verb should be 'indicates'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: Every one of the shortlisted applicants (1)/ were instructed
sentence: to submit additional documentation (2)/ prior to the commencement of the evaluation process (3)/ conducted by the oversight committee. (4)
explanation: 'Every one of + plural noun' is singular, so it should be 'was instructed'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Despite clear evidence of mismanagement, the officials (1)/ were failing to implement corrective measures (2)/ in accordance with regulatory mandates (3)/ and public accountability standards. (4)
explanation: A completed past failure needs the simple past 'failed', not the past continuous 'were failing'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: It was not until much later (1)/ that the inconsistencies in the financial reports (2)/ were brought to light by the whistleblower, (3)/ whose testimony proved more reliable than anyone else. (4)
explanation: The comparison must be between like items: 'more reliable than that of anyone else' (or 'than anyone else's').

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The fact that citizens have no remedy available (1)/ when
sentence: environmental breaches are ignored at the ministerial level (2)/ highlight a broader decline in (3)/ constitutional accountability. (4)
explanation: The head of the subject is the singular noun 'The fact', so the verb must be 'highlights', not 'highlight'; the intervening 'that'-clause does not change the number.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The revised legislative framework is capable for addressing (1)/ the deep-rooted systemic inequalities (2)/ that have persisted across marginalised communities (3)/ for over three decades. (4)
explanation: 'Capable' is followed by 'of' + gerund, so it should be 'capable of addressing', not 'capable for addressing'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The initiatives praised by the committee (1)/ are not only designed to modernise reporting systems (2)/ but also improving transparency in funding distribution (3)/ across all districts. (4)
explanation: 'Not only ... but also' must join parallel structures; 'designed to modernise' requires 'but also to improve transparency', not 'improving'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Had the committee not postponed the review, (1)/ the institution would have had a better chance (2)/ to scrutinising the financial irregularities (3)/ before the annual audit commenced. (4)
explanation: 'Chance' takes either 'to' + base verb or 'of' + gerund, so 'to scrutinising' should be 'to scrutinise' (or 'of scrutinising').

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The degree to which the policy drew public opposition (1)/ signals not only institutional failure (2)/ but also that civil society has (3)/ grown increasingly assertive in its demands. (4)
explanation: 'Not only' is followed by a noun phrase ('institutional failure'), so 'but also' must also take a noun phrase (e.g., 'but also the growing assertiveness of civil society'), not a 'that'-clause.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Having completed the initial draft hastily, (1)/ the revised proposal was then forwarded (2)/ to the senior consultants for review (3)/ who had previously raised structural objections. (4)
explanation: The participle 'Having completed' needs an agent as subject, but the passive clause makes 'the revised proposal' the subject, creating a dangling modifier; it should be 'the committee then forwarded the revised proposal'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The manager could not decide whether to approve the merger (1)/ or if the announcement were merely a diversion (2)/ intended to calm investors (3)/ after the recent financial losses. (4)/
explanation: 'Whether' must be balanced by 'or whether' (or a bare 'or'), not 'or if'; also the indicative 'was' is required rather than 'were'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The discrepancy between predicted and observed results (1)/ raised questions not only about the methodology (2)/ but also about the premises that (3)/ underlied the entire proposal. (4)/
explanation: 'Underlie' is an irregular verb whose past form is 'underlay' (past participle 'underlain'), so 'underlied' is wrong.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The committee recommended that the proposal is reconsidered (1)/ in light of emerging fiscal constraints (2)/ and broader regulatory implications (3)/ across multiple jurisdictions. (4)/
explanation: After 'recommended that', the subjunctive base form is required: 'that the proposal be reconsidered', not 'is reconsidered'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Much of what seems to be coordination (1) / among the regulatory bodies and private stakeholders (2) / are, in reality, coincidental overlaps (3) / arising from differing mandates (4).
explanation: The subject 'Much of what seems to be coordination' is singular, so the verb must be 'is', not 'are'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The authority’s choice to delay the rollout (1)/ was linked
sentence: partly to pressure from the industry (2)/ and partly because of legal uncertainty (3)/ related to the latest amendments. (4)
explanation: Parallelism requires 'partly to pressure ... and partly to legal uncertainty'; 'partly because of' breaks the structure after 'was linked to'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The certification module was structured (1)/ to make the participants capable to resolve (2)/ high-risk compliance issues effectively (3)/ in cross-border financial transactions. (4)/
explanation: 'Capable' is never followed by an infinitive; the correct form is 'capable of resolving'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Had the recommendations been implemented (1)/ and fiscal irregularities addressed, the commission might have had (2)/ prevented the subsequent collapse (3)/ of the institution. (4)/
explanation: The modal perfect is 'might have prevented'; the extra 'had' in 'might have had prevented' is ungrammatical.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The spokesperson stated that the issue had been addressed (1)/ although no official clarification (2)/ regarding the procedural lapse (3)/ were circulated to the stakeholders. (4)/
explanation: The singular subject 'no official clarification' requires the singular verb 'was circulated'; the prepositional phrase does not affect agreement.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The guideline seeks to neither prosecute minor violations (1)/ nor to overlook repeated breaches (2)/ arising from procedural confusion (3)/ rather than deliberate misconduct. (4)
explanation: After 'seeks to', the correlative must join parallel base verbs: 'to neither prosecute ... nor overlook'; the second 'to' destroys the parallelism.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The speed with which the markets collapsed (1)/ caught not only the regulators but also the investors (2)/ off guard
sentence: who had been predicting (3)/ a period of sustained growth. (4)
explanation: The relative clause 'who had been predicting' is misplaced far from its antecedent 'the investors'; it should immediately follow that noun.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The managing director together with the advisory board (1)/ were instrumental in negotiating the merger (2)/ with international stakeholders (3)/ and regulatory authorities. (4)/
explanation: 'Together with' is an additive connective that does not change the number of the subject, so the singular 'The managing director' requires 'was'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: That the report overlooked several underlying causes (1)/ behind the public unrest were surprising (2)/ given the volume of evidence (3)/ collected over the past few months. (4)
explanation: A 'that'-clause used as subject is singular, so the verb must be 'was surprising', not 'were surprising'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The symposium on autonomous systems (1)/ underscored an urgent need of robust ethical frameworks (2)/ to anticipate unforeseen consequences (3)/ of machine decision-making. (4)/
explanation: The noun 'need' takes the preposition 'for' when followed by a thing required: 'an urgent need for robust ethical frameworks'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: If the policy were to be implemented nationwide (1)/ it would necessitate that every regional office (2)/ conducts a comprehensive audit (3)/ within a period of six months. (4)/
explanation: 'Necessitate that' triggers the subjunctive, so it must be 'every regional office conduct', not 'conducts'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: It was at the diplomatic conclave in Zurich (1)/ where the bilateral accord was formally endorsed, (2)/ thereby inaugurating (3)/ a renewed phase of strategic cooperation. (4)/
explanation: In the cleft structure 'It was at ... that ...', the connector must be 'that', not 'where'; so '(2) where the bilateral accord was formally endorsed' is wrong.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The committee’s recommendation, notwithstanding its ambiguity, (1)/ were considered by the reviewers (2)/ to prioritise procedural compliance (3)/ over substantive reform. (4)
explanation: The subject 'The committee's recommendation' is singular, and the intervening phrase 'notwithstanding its ambiguity' does not change it, so 'were considered' must be 'was considered'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Only after the final audit report was submitted (1)/ did the committee realise (2)/ that the estimates, although well- documented, (3)/ has omitted indirect liabilities. (4)
explanation: The omission happened before the past-tense realisation, so the past perfect 'had omitted' is required instead of 'has omitted'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: That none of the applicants considered the policy fair (1)/ is hardly shocking given (2)/ that neither the supervisor nor the HR officer (3)/ were informed in advance. (4)
explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'the HR officer', which is singular, so 'were informed' should be 'was informed'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The committee’s recommendations on climate policy (1)/ has been considered by multiple governments (2)/ as overly ambitious and impractical (3)/ in certain contexts. (4)
explanation: The plural subject 'recommendations' needs 'have been considered', not 'has been considered'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The merger was announced so abruptly (1)/ that it shocked not only the board members (2)/ but also to the investors (3)/ who had been expecting gradual transition. (4)/
explanation: 'Not only ... but also' must join parallel elements; since 'not only' is followed by the object 'the board members', 'but also to the investors' wrongly adds 'to'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Were she to have submitted the files on time, (1)/ the delay could have been (2)/ avoided much sooner than it actually was, (3)/ preventing unnecessary confusion. (4)/
explanation: The comparison is illogical: the delay was never avoided, so 'much sooner than it actually was' is faulty; the unreal conditional needs simply 'the delay could have been avoided'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The belief that the instructions are merely advisory (1) / instead of mandatory have caused (2) / repeated lapses in adherence (3) / across multiple departments. (4)
explanation: The head subject is the singular noun 'The belief', so the verb must be 'has caused', not 'have caused'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Seldom had the tribunal entertained an appeal (1)/ so lacking in substance, nor so plainly designed (2)/ to invite publicity rather than justice. (3)/ No error (4)/
explanation: The two modifiers of 'appeal' should be joined by 'or' ('so lacking in substance, or so plainly designed'); 'nor' is incorrect as no second negative clause follows.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Not only the chairman but also the members (1)/ has been charged with violating (2)/ the rules mentioned in the official notice (3)/ during the proceedings. (4)/
explanation: With 'not only ... but also', the verb agrees with the second subject 'the members', so 'has been charged' must be 'have been charged'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Despite the warning signs, (1)/ the project lead had failed recognising (2)/ the critical flaws in the initial design (3)/ before the prototype was approved. (4)
explanation: 'Fail' is followed by an infinitive, so 'had failed recognising' should be 'had failed to recognise'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: It was not until the audit findings (1)/ were submitted to the oversight committee (2)/ did the corporation initiated (3)/ a comprehensive internal review. (4)/
explanation: With the cleft 'It was not until ... that', no inversion is used and the verb must be finite: 'that the corporation initiated', not 'did the corporation initiated'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The organisation requires a detailed feedback (1)/ from each department (2)/ before finalising its restructuring plan (3)/ for the next financial year. (4)/
explanation: 'Feedback' is an uncountable noun and cannot take the article 'a'; it should be 'detailed feedback'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The arbitrator concluded that the (1)/ dispute centred on the principle (2)/ issue of property rights rather than (3)/ any procedural irregularity. (4)/
explanation: The adjective meaning 'main' is 'principal'; 'principle' is a noun, so 'principle issue' should be 'principal issue'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The merger was deferred indefinitely (1)/ owing of the failure to reach (2)/ a consensus among the principal (3)/ shareholders of both corporations. (4)
explanation: The fixed expression is 'owing to', not 'owing of'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: All that is required for the motion to succeed (1)/ are a two-thirds vote (2)/ and approval from the chairperson (3)/ to validate the decision. (4)/
explanation: 'All that is required' is a singular subject phrase, so the verb should be 'is a two-thirds vote', matching the singular 'is required'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The committees submitted their individual advices (1)/ to the ministerial panel (2)/ before the policy document (3)/ was tabled in Parliament. (4)
explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable and has no plural form, so 'their individual advices' should be 'their individual advice' (or 'pieces of advice').

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: Hardly had the memorandum been circulated (1)/ than dissenting opinions were voiced (2)/ by senior analysts (3)/
sentence: during the plenary session. (4)/
explanation: 'Hardly' is correlated with 'when', not 'than', so '(2)' should read 'when dissenting opinions were voiced'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: No sooner had the policy been announced (1)/ when the opposition not only criticized it (2)/ but also (3)/ demanded its immediate withdrawal. (4)
explanation: 'No sooner' is followed by 'than', not 'when', so '(2)' should begin 'than the opposition'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Rarely if ever have there been a time (1)/ when dissent was met (2)/ with such institutional disregard (3)/ as in the present administration. (4)
explanation: In 'there' sentences the verb agrees with the following singular noun 'a time', so it should be 'has there been a time'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Much efforts have been made (1)/ by the development team (2)/ to reduce the application's loading time (3)/ without compromising features. (4)/
explanation: 'Effort' is countable here, so 'Much efforts' is wrong; it should be 'Many efforts' (or 'Much effort').

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: She delivered (1)/ a comprehensive overview of the proposal (2)/ but failed to substantiate her claims (3)/ with sufficient evidences. (4)/
explanation: 'Evidence' is an uncountable noun and has no plural form, so 'sufficient evidences' should be 'sufficient evidence'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: It is essential that every applicant submits (1)/ their documents before the deadline (2)/ and that no forms (3)/ are left incomplete. (4)/
explanation: After 'It is essential that', the subjunctive (base form) is required: 'every applicant submit', not 'submits'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The higher the office was (1)/ the more pressing became the need (2)/ for prudence, propriety, and (3)/ avoiding of early disclosure. (4)
explanation: Parallelism with the nouns 'prudence, propriety' requires the noun 'avoidance of early disclosure', not the gerund phrase 'avoiding of'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The revised guideline states (1)/ that every employee must comply with (2)/ the conduct policy (3)/ regardless of their designation. (4)/
explanation: 'Every employee' is singular, so the pronoun must be singular: 'regardless of his or her designation', not 'their'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Each of the shortlisted candidates (1)/ have submitted their credentials (2)/ prior to the final interview (3)/ conducted last week. (4)/
explanation: 'Each of + plural noun' takes a singular verb, so 'have submitted' should be 'has submitted'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The apprentices were directed (1)/ to finalize the documentation expeditiously (2)/ and submit it (3)/ in a legible handwriting. (4)/
explanation: 'Handwriting' is uncountable and used in a general sense, so no article is used: 'in legible handwriting'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The library provides access to (1)/ extensive collection of journals (2)/ and research databases (3)/ for postgraduate scholars. (4)/
explanation: The singular countable noun 'collection' needs an indefinite article: 'an extensive collection of journals'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The new policy was more superior (1)/ to its predecessor
sentence: (2)/ in terms of implementation strategy (3)/ and fiscal transparency. (4)/
explanation: 'Superior' is already comparative in sense, so 'more superior' is a double comparative; use 'was superior to'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The workshop aims at providing participants (1)/ with useful informations (2)/ about digital marketing (3)/ in the
sentence: current era. (4)/
explanation: 'Information' is uncountable and has no plural, so 'useful informations' should be 'useful information'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The workshop aims at providing entrepreneurs (1)/ with practical advices (2)/ on scaling operations (3)/ in emerging markets. (4)/
explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable; 'practical advices' should be 'practical advice'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The research division (1)/ consists specialists (2)/ in analytics,
sentence: forecasting, and strategy (3)/ across multiple sectors. (4)/
explanation: 'Consist' is always followed by 'of', so it should be 'consists of specialists'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The manager insisted (1)/ that every employee must submits the form (2)/ before the deadline (3)/ without any exceptions. (4)/
explanation: After 'insisted that', the structure is 'should + V1' or the subjunctive base form: 'every employee should submit / submit the form', not 'must submits'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: The majority of the evidence submitted (1)/ to the tribunal have been (2)/ deemed admissible by (3)/ the presiding judge. (4)
explanation: The main subject is the uncountable noun 'evidence', so the verb must be singular: 'has been deemed'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: No sooner the verdict was delivered (1)/ than the defence counsel (2)/ filed an application (3)/ for an immediate stay. (4)/
explanation: 'No sooner' at the start of a sentence requires inversion: 'No sooner was the verdict delivered than...'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: Little did the board knew (1)/ about the concealed risks (2)/ when it endorsed the acquisition (3)/ late last year. (4)/
explanation: With the negative inversion 'Little did', the base form of the verb follows: 'Little did the board know'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: Many informations were shared (1)/ during the seminar (2)/
sentence: about emerging technologies (3)/ in healthcare. (4)/
explanation: 'Information' is uncountable, so it must be 'Much information was shared', not 'Many informations were shared'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
sentence: It’s strategic location (1)/ renders the port (2)/ indispensable to regional (3)/ maritime trade routes. (4)/
explanation: The possessive determiner is 'Its'; 'It's' means 'it is', which does not fit before 'strategic location'.

prompt: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: Rarely does he goes (1)/ to the office (2)/ on weekends (3)/
sentence: due to workload. (4)/
explanation: After the inversion 'Rarely does he', the main verb stays in the base form: 'Rarely does he go'.

sentence: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A In those allotted minutes the directors have the freedom to interpret the segments in their own unique way. B The play has been divided into segments of 10 minutes each by the directors. C Eight young directors, over 50 actors and one landmark play-Hayavadana. D This unique collaboration is a tribute to the playwright Girish Karnad.
explanation: C introduces the participants and the play, D identifies it as a tribute to Karnad, B explains the division into 10-minute segments, and A follows up on 'those allotted minutes', giving CDBA.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: He lived close to / the train station, / yet travelled by bus.
explanation: 'Lived close to the train station' and the contrast marker 'yet travelled by bus' are both idiomatic and grammatically correct, so the sentence has no error.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Dan needed help / to get the / tight coat of him.
explanation: Possession by a person is shown with a possessive adjective, so 'the tight coat of him' must be 'his tight coat'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I, you and she/ have been working happily/ in the same company and in the same branch/ for the last nine years.
options: in the same company and in the same branch
explanation: When pronouns of all three persons are joined in a positive statement, the order is 2-3-1: 'You, she and I'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. It takes me an hour to get to work at the moment, but when the new road is finished it be much quicker.
options: but when the new road is finished
It takes me an hour to get to work
explanation: The main clause of a future time clause needs a finite verb: 'it will be much quicker', not the bare 'it be'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: We should sorted out / the problem ourselves / rather than depending / on the third party.
explanation: A modal like 'should' is always followed by the base form, so 'should sorted out' must be 'should sort out'.

prompt: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: When I returned to the office, / no work was left / as my friend Rahul / has done everything.
options: When I returned to the office
explanation: Of two past actions, the earlier one takes the past perfect, so 'has done everything' must be 'had done everything'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. In this lock-down period every worker in the factory has started bring their own lunch.
explanation: 'Start' is followed by a gerund or infinitive, so 'has started bring' should be 'has started bringing' (or 'to bring').

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Craze for a thing that are not easily available in our country is a common phenomenon.
explanation: The relative pronoun's verb agrees with its antecedent 'a thing', which is singular, so it should be 'thing that is not easily'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He was unable / to help me because / he had been failed / to arrange the money.
explanation: 'Fail' is intransitive here and takes no passive form; the correct phrasing is 'he had failed to arrange the money'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. No sooner had Kavya started her online class that the web connection was lost.
explanation: 'No sooner' is always correlated with 'than', not 'that': 'No sooner had Kavya started ... than the web connection was lost'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The reason for visiting Meerut was because my mother needed to be looked after.
explanation: 'The reason ... was because' is redundant; the correct construction is 'The reason ... was that'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: This renowned / university provide / research opportunities / for students.
explanation: The singular subject 'This renowned university' needs the singular verb 'provides'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Each one of the children in a nursery class require individual attention.
explanation: 'Each one of the children' is a singular subject, so the verb must be 'requires individual attention'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The girl lay down / on the bed / besides her mother / and went to sleep.
explanation: 'Beside' means 'by the side of', while 'besides' means 'in addition to'; here it should be 'beside her mother'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: His son-in-laws / have enhanced / his business / within a short period.
explanation: In compound nouns of the type noun+preposition+noun, the first word is pluralised: 'His sons-in-law'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The city turned out / to be very / different to what / he had expected.
explanation: The adjective 'different' takes the preposition 'from', so it should be 'different from what he had expected'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He often / persists to ask / awkward questions / at the board meetings.
explanation: 'Persist' is followed by 'in' + gerund, so 'persists to ask' must be 'persists in asking'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Scarcely had I / started reading / the paper / then the doorbell rang.
explanation: 'Scarcely/Hardly had ...' is completed by 'when', not 'then': 'when the doorbell rang'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Mr. Das, my friend / and Principal / of this college, / have retired.
explanation: 'My friend and Principal of this college' describes one person, Mr. Das, so the verb must be singular: 'has retired'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options. If there is no error, select No error.
sentence: Everything has became very expensive these days.
explanation: After 'has', the past participle is required, so 'has became' must be 'has become'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: This dog seems / to be very ferocious, / otherwise, / it is harmless.
explanation: The sense is contrast, not alternative consequence, so 'otherwise' should be 'but'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. When there were a strong wind, the pine trees made sad, eerie sounds.
explanation: The subject 'a strong wind' is singular, so the introductory 'there' clause needs 'was' — 'When there was a strong wind'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options. If there is no error, select No error.
sentence: They made her as the Chairperson of their bank.
explanation: Verbs like 'make', 'appoint', 'elect', 'call' do not take 'as' before the complement: 'They made her the Chairperson'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options. If there is no error, select No error.
sentence: What is the function of the kidney in the body?
explanation: The sentence is correct; 'the kidney' as a singular noun with 'the' properly denotes the organ as a class.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: You should / avail this opportunity / to demonstrate / your skills.
explanation: 'Avail' requires a reflexive pronoun and 'of': 'avail yourself of this opportunity'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: If you have / remained calm / you could have / saved the situation.
explanation: With 'could have saved' in the main clause, the if-clause needs the past perfect: 'If you had remained calm'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The allies / of the government / decided to / withdrew all support.
explanation: After 'decided to', the base form is required: 'withdraw all support', not 'withdrew'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Two flyovers have been propose in the new plan to decongest M.G. Road.
explanation: The passive needs the past participle: 'have been proposed', not 'have been propose'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The postman / delivers the letters / through hand, / door to door.
explanation: The fixed idiom for means of delivery is 'by hand', not 'through hand'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options. If there is no error, select No error.
sentence: No one inform me that you would be absent.
explanation: The reported clause 'you would be absent' shows past reference, so the verb should be 'informed'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My father give up / smoking when / I was twelve / years old.
explanation: The past time marker 'when I was twelve' requires the past form 'gave up'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She has been working with me on this project from two years.
explanation: A period of time with a perfect continuous tense takes 'for', so it should be 'for two years'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She watched / the thief who / steal the purse / in the bus.
explanation: The relative clause describes a past action, so it needs 'stole the purse'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My grandmother is quite concerned to my progress at school.
explanation: 'Concerned' in the sense of worried takes 'about': 'concerned about my progress'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. A tallest man that I have ever seen works in our coal mine.
explanation: A superlative takes the definite article: 'The tallest man that I have ever seen'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Bhanu finished to read such a thick book in just two days.
explanation: 'Finish' is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive: 'finished reading'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Have you / ever spoke / to anyone / about your problems?
explanation: The present perfect needs the past participle: 'Have you ever spoken'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Everybody stared / when me / entered the / drawing room.
explanation: The pronoun is the subject of 'entered', so the nominative form is needed: 'when I entered'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The manager / took him / at task / for his negligence.
explanation: The correct idiom is 'take (someone) to task', meaning to reprimand; 'at task' is wrong.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Daniel sat on / his new bike / and went afar / a ride.
explanation: The idiomatic expression is 'went for a ride'; 'afar' is not used with 'ride'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The more harder / you work, / the better / it will be.
explanation: 'More harder' is a double comparative; the correct form is 'The harder you work'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Before take this medicine you should consult a doctor.
explanation: 'Before' here is a preposition, so it must be followed by a gerund: 'Before taking this medicine'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. A confluence is a place when two or more rivers meet.
explanation: A relative clause describing a 'place' needs 'where', not 'when': 'a place where two or more rivers meet'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He gave such a long speech but everybody felt bored.
explanation: 'Such' must be completed by 'that' (such a long speech that everybody felt bored), so 'such' is wrongly used with 'but'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The three of them shouted out to each another when the train started moving.
explanation: For more than two persons the reciprocal pronoun is 'one another', and 'each another' is never correct.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. A large number of worker have started walking home.
explanation: 'A large number of' is followed by a plural countable noun: 'of workers'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He was not able to give many time to his research.
explanation: 'Time' here is uncountable, so it takes 'much', not 'many': 'much time'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Your name / precedes before / mine / in the list.
explanation: 'Precede' already means 'come before', so 'before' is superfluous: 'Your name precedes mine'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. A large amount of money he invested were wasted.
explanation: The subject 'A large amount of money' is singular, so the verb must be 'was wasted'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I am sorry I haven’t learnt the poem at heart.
explanation: The fixed idiom is 'learn by heart', not 'learn at heart'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He went / to the bed / with a / slight fever.
explanation: In the idiomatic phrase 'go to bed' no article is used, so 'to the bed' is wrong.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: There was enough evidence to convict him on selling of fake medicines.
explanation: The correct collocation is 'convict him of selling'; 'on selling of' wrongly adds prepositions.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The tired and vexed travellers waiting at the airport for a long time.
explanation: The sentence has no finite verb; the participle must become a tensed verb: 'were waiting at the airport'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I shall buy this book if you like it or not.
explanation: With the '...or not' construction, 'whether' must be used instead of 'if': 'whether you like it or not'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. No one have ever visited this place before.
explanation: 'No one' is singular and takes a singular verb: 'No one has ever visited'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Although this is a narrowest street, many large trucks can enter it.
explanation: A superlative takes 'the', not 'a'; here the sense requires 'a narrow street'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I can explain you the reason for the delay in executing your order.
explanation: 'Explain' takes 'to' before the indirect object: 'I can explain to you the reason'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Zoya won the first prize in the race unless she stumbled and fell.
explanation: 'Unless' (negative condition) makes no sense here; a contrast conjunction like 'though/even though she stumbled' is required.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Laws and rules are made to safeguarding our rights and protect us.
explanation: After 'are made to', the base form of the verb is required, and it must be parallel with 'protect', so 'safeguarding' should be 'safeguard'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: We yet / have time / to catch / the bus.
explanation: 'Yet' is not used in affirmative statements of this type; the correct adverb is 'still' — 'We still have time'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The man played the flute and led all the mouse out of the town.
explanation: 'All' requires a plural noun, so the irregular plural 'mice' must replace 'mouse'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: This jewellery box is made from silver and is an antique piece.
explanation: 'Made of' is used when the original material is still visible in the product; 'made from' implies the material has been transformed, so it should be 'made of silver'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Poor people have run down of food supplies during the lockdown.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb for exhausting a supply is 'run out of', not 'run down of'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: No one of them came to the inauguration of our new factory.
explanation: 'No one' is not followed by 'of'; with a plural group the correct pronoun is 'None of them'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Neither Sam nor I are interested in attending the meeting.
explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'I', so 'are interested' should be 'am interested'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Did you told him about the new plot that you have bought?
explanation: After the auxiliary 'did', the base form of the verb is required — 'Did you tell him'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: An eight years old girl has made this beautiful painting.
explanation: A numeral adjective used before a noun stays singular and hyphenated — 'an eight-year-old girl'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: We must plan how can we cope with the present situation.
explanation: An embedded (indirect) question keeps normal word order, so 'how can we' should be 'how we can'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She has been a member of this club since it’s formation.
explanation: 'It's' is the contraction of 'it is'; the possessive determiner 'its' is needed — 'since its formation'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The girl besides you in high heels is my younger sister.
explanation: 'Beside' means 'next to', while 'besides' means 'in addition to', so it should be 'The girl beside you'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She asked me where had I gone for dinner with my fiance.
explanation: In indirect speech the interrogative inversion is dropped, so 'where had I' should be 'where I had'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He thinks that he can get away among lying and cheating.
explanation: The fixed idiom is 'get away with', not 'get away among' — so it should be 'with lying'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: You must be careful about what you say as you meet her.
explanation: The clause states a point of time, so the time conjunction 'when' is needed instead of 'as'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The venue for the wedding have not yet been finalised.
explanation: The head subject is the singular 'venue' ('for the wedding' is only a modifier), so the verb must be 'has not yet been finalised'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: They will be ready leaving for the airport in an hour.
explanation: The adjective 'ready' is followed by an infinitive, so it should be 'ready to leave'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Three hours will have passed when the bell will ring.
explanation: A clause introduced by 'when' does not take a future tense; it should be 'when the bell rings'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Whole country applauded the courage of our soldiers.
explanation: 'Whole' preceding a singular noun requires the definite article — 'The whole country'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He has shattered his neighbour’s window by purpose.
explanation: The idiom is 'on purpose', not 'by purpose'; deliberate action takes the fixed preposition 'on'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He loses his tempers on the slightest provocation.
explanation: 'Lose one's temper' is a fixed expression with the singular noun 'temper', so 'his tempers' is wrong.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Let us think how can we solve the problem amiably.
explanation: An indirect (embedded) question takes normal word order, so 'how can we' must be 'how we can'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The concert has started when he reached the venue.
explanation: The concert starting happened before he reached, so the earlier past action needs the past perfect 'had started'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I didn’t knew you had gone to Goa for a vacation.
explanation: After the auxiliary 'did/didn't' the bare infinitive is used, so it should be 'I didn't know'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The captain scored a century in a second innings.
explanation: Ordinals take the definite article, so 'in a second innings' must be 'in the second innings'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I looked him at the eye and told him all I knew.
explanation: The fixed idiom is 'look someone in the eye', not 'at the eye'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I want you to complete this work by two days.
explanation: A deadline/period of completion takes 'in' or 'within', so 'by two days' should be 'in two days'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The small cafe at the end of the road is her.
explanation: A possessive pronoun standing alone is needed, so 'is her' must be 'is hers'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: As such you need any money, just write to me.
explanation: The clause states a condition, so 'As such you' should be 'If you' (or 'In case you').

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Do you mind lending me your book for a hour?
explanation: 'Hour' begins with a vowel sound (silent h), so it takes 'an hour'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Aren’t you such young to travel by yourself?
explanation: Before an adjective + infinitive, 'too' is used, not 'such'; it should be 'too young to travel'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: This is only the decent dress that I have.
explanation: 'Only' must follow the article and modify the noun phrase: 'the only decent dress'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She is not as smart as I think at first.
explanation: 'At first' refers to past time, so the verb must be past simple: 'as I thought at first'.
