prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The seat which you are sitting on is my.
explanation: A predicative possessive requires the pronoun 'mine', not the determiner 'my'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: The need today is for both sides / to introspect and re-examine the issue carefully / and resolve it amicably.
options: to introspect and re-examine the issue carefully
The need today is for both sides
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct, with parallel infinitives 'to introspect', 're-examine' and 'resolve'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: The energy required / for perform various functions of the body / is obtained from food.
options: for perform various functions of the body
explanation: A preposition must be followed by a gerund, so it should be 'for performing' (or 'to perform') various functions.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: She managed the company / so well that it is made / a huge profit that year.
options: so well that it is made
explanation: 'Made a huge profit' is active; the passive 'is made' is wrong and the past tense is required: 'so well that it made'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: The monkeys swinged / on the branches and / jumped over the compound wall.
explanation: 'Swing' is an irregular verb whose past form is 'swung', not 'swinged'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My brother lost / his job during the lockdown, / but he had got / a new job now.
explanation: 'Now' signals present perfect, so 'he had got' should be 'he has got'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He will be leaving / home at 8 a.m. / to beating / the office rush hour.
explanation: The infinitive of purpose is required after 'leaving', so 'to beating' must be 'to beat'; 'to' as an infinitive marker takes the base verb.

prompt: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Every participant gave so outstanding performance that it became difficult to choose the winner.
explanation: 'So' cannot modify an adjective+noun combination; with a singular noun the correct correlative is 'such an outstanding performance ... that'.

prompt: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Doctors say that home isolation is far more effective than hospitalise in cases of mild infection.
explanation: The comparison must be between two comparable nouns, so the verb 'hospitalise' should be the noun 'hospitalisation' to match 'home isolation'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".
sentence: If conventional arrangements and/ patterns are made more scarcer, other/ arrangements and patterns will spring up.
options: patterns are made more scarcer, other
arrangements and patterns will spring up.
explanation: 'Scarcer' is already comparative, so adding 'more' creates a double comparative; it should be 'more scarce' or simply 'scarcer'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".
sentence: It's 4 p.m. local time and quite a/ large crowd has gathered from yesterday/ evening around the giant stage.
options: It's 4 p.m. local time and quite a
large crowd has gathered from yesterday
explanation: With the present perfect and a point of time, 'since' is used, not 'from': 'has gathered since yesterday evening'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: Atmospheric rivers are long, narrow bands of moisture in the atmosphere that extends from the tropics to higher latitudes.
options: of moisture in the atmosphere that extends from the
Atmospheric rivers are long, narrow bands
explanation: The relative clause refers to the plural antecedent 'bands', so the verb must be 'extend', not 'extends'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: A study finds that the average staff cost at a public sector bank is high than that at its private sector counterpart.
options: a public sector bank is high than that at
A study finds that the average staff cost at
explanation: A comparison with 'than' requires the comparative degree, so 'high than' must become 'higher than'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. This was no strange sight / to the boy by that time, / for he had neither gun or spear.
options: to the boy by that time
for he had neither gun or spear.
explanation: 'Neither' is correlated with 'nor', not 'or': 'he had neither gun nor spear'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: Plastic debris in the ocean can become coated with algae and other marine microbes that produces a chemical scent.
options: marine microbes that produces a chemical scent.
Plastic debris in the ocean can become
explanation: The antecedent of 'that' is the plural 'algae and other marine microbes', so the verb should be 'produce'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".
sentence: The London-based Brodsky/ Quartet, meanwhile, is one of/ the world's leading string quartet.
explanation: 'One of' must be followed by a plural noun, so 'string quartet' should be 'string quartets'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: When we cook garlic, the sulphide molecules raise into the air and fill the room with their pleasing aroma.
options: When we cook garlic, the sulphide
and fill the room with their pleasing aroma.
explanation: 'Raise' is transitive and needs an object; the intransitive verb 'rise' is required — 'molecules rise into the air'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".
sentence: A witness had seen a youth, / perhaps aged young as/ ten or eleven, acting suspiciously.
options: A witness had seen a youth
explanation: The comparison of equality needs the 'as ... as' structure: 'perhaps as young as ten or eleven'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".
sentence: Today, in fit of frenzied rage and / jealousy, you would have/ killed me, your brother.
options: Today, in fit of frenzied rage and
explanation: The countable singular noun 'fit' needs the indefinite article: 'in a fit of frenzied rage'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. They know they will face / either a swift backlash / or deafening silence.
explanation: The correlative pair 'either ... or' is correctly used and the two joined elements are parallel noun phrases, so the sentence is grammatically sound.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. Once I run in / the Sonoran Desert in Arizona / after a huge rain event.
explanation: 'Once' here refers to a completed past occasion, so the past simple 'ran' is required instead of 'run'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".
sentence: And it just recently awarded/ a million-dollar contract/ that reeks of corruption.
explanation: 'Just' and 'recently' convey the same idea, making 'just recently' redundant; one of the two adverbs should be dropped.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: There is evidence that much too technology can lead to a loss of child development opportunities.
options: There is evidence that much too
explanation: Before an uncountable noun the correct quantifier order is 'too much technology'; 'much too' only intensifies adjectives/adverbs.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. You care for him / even more than for myself, / he cried bitterly.
explanation: A reflexive pronoun cannot follow a preposition in a comparison with a different subject; it should be 'even more than for me'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: Our hands have been crucial tools for finding and eat food, and helping us navigate the world.
options: tools for finding and eat food
and helping us navigate the world.
explanation: Items joined after the preposition 'for' must be parallel gerunds: 'for finding and eating food'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: Fashion might not be first thing that comes to mind when we think of isolation strategies.
options: thing that comes to mind when
explanation: An ordinal like 'first' takes the definite article, so it should be 'might not be the first thing'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: As per the study, mosquito-borne dengue fever infects little 400 million people annually.
explanation: 'Little' cannot modify a number; the sense required is 'nearly/almost 400 million people'. So 'dengue fever infects little' is wrong.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence are given as options. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. He has been / told many a times to / mind his manners.
explanation: 'Many a' is always followed by a singular noun, so it must be 'many a time', not 'many a times'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: The recent discoveries have risen hopes about possible applications.
explanation: 'Rise' is intransitive and takes no object; the transitive verb is needed here, so it should be 'have raised hopes'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’. In the five next years, the migration will surely stop.
explanation: The ordinal/general-order word precedes the cardinal number, so the correct order is 'In the next five years'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: No doubt, human minds are good on predicting the worst.
explanation: The fixed collocation is 'good at' doing something, not 'good on'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: I will never judge you for yours impromptu performance.
explanation: 'Yours' is a possessive pronoun and cannot precede a noun; the possessive adjective 'your' is required before 'impromptu performance'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: India has turned 70 years older as a Republic.
explanation: Age is expressed with the positive degree: '70 years old', not the comparative 'older', since no comparison is being made.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: I just don’t like the themes of todays music.
explanation: The possessive of 'today' needs an apostrophe: 'today's music'.

prompt: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.
sentence: It turns out that my father isn’t alone.
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct: 'It turns out that' introduces a noun clause and 'alone' is used correctly as a predicative adjective.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Washington Irving’s writing career started at / the tender age of nineteen when he joined / his brother Peter’s newspaper The Morning Chronical / as journalist.
options: his brother Peter’s newspaper The Morning Chronical
Washington Irving’s writing career started at
the tender age of nineteen when he joined
explanation: A singular countable noun after 'as' denoting a profession needs the article: 'as a journalist'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that contains the error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. With reference of your letter, the organisation wishes to hire you for the security services.
options: the organisation wishes to hire you
explanation: The fixed phrase is 'with reference to', not 'with reference of'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: The food container / is not enough big to meet / the demands of the affected people.
options: is not enough big to meet
the demands of the affected people.
explanation: 'Enough' follows the adjective it modifies, so the correct form is 'is not big enough to meet'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that contains the error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. In this world of competitions, every one of us is required to plan our course careful.
options: every one of us is required
explanation: The verb 'plan' needs an adverb, not an adjective: 'to plan our course carefully'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that contains the error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. By virtue off the power given to the leader, the followers accepted his decision.
options: the power given to the leader
explanation: The prepositional phrase is 'by virtue of'; 'off' is incorrect.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Hurray! Here is the toy / what I was looking for / as my birthday gift.
explanation: 'What' cannot be used with an expressed antecedent ('the toy'); the relative pronoun 'that/which' is required.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: He speaks pleasantly / with her yesterday / evening but not today.
explanation: 'Yesterday' signals past indefinite tense, so the verb must be 'spoke', not the present 'speaks'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that contains the error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The soldier met a fearless death fighting on behalf at his country.
options: fighting on behalf at his country
explanation: The fixed phrase is 'on behalf of', not 'on behalf at'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: A owl was / hooting throughout / the night.
explanation: 'Owl' begins with a vowel sound, so the article must be 'An owl', not 'A owl'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: A crocodile / was swimming / in a river.
explanation: The article usage, past continuous tense and preposition are all correct, so the sentence has no error.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Can you please / pass me a sweater? / It’s going to be / the cold day today.
explanation: A non-specific description of the weather takes the indefinite article: 'a cold day today'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.
sentence: This boy / is cleverest / of all / in the class.
explanation: A superlative degree adjective must be preceded by 'the', so it should be 'is the cleverest'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The politician was accused of accepting bribes and lied about it to the public.
explanation: After 'accused of', both items must be gerunds for parallelism: 'accepting bribes and lying about it'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: They were laid / in the sun / the entire morning / till Sudharshan came.
explanation: 'Lay' (laid) is transitive; the intransitive sense of reclining requires 'They were lying in the sun'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The team of scientists were conducting experiments to test their hypothesis.
explanation: The main subject is the singular noun 'team', so the verb must be 'was conducting'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The poor undergoes several problems in life that could be solved with money.
explanation: 'The + adjective' ('the poor') denotes a class of people and takes a plural verb: 'The poor undergo'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The lack of mutual bonding was conspicuous from their shody body language in the marriage party.
explanation: 'Shody' is a misspelling; the correct spelling is 'shoddy'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The government has been accused in not doing enough to combat climate change.
explanation: The verb 'accuse' takes the fixed preposition 'of', so it should be 'accused of not doing'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I brought / an apple from / a place you recommended / me earlier.
explanation: 'Recommend' requires 'to' before the indirect object: 'a place you recommended to me earlier'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Can you please / open a door? / I can hear / somebody knocking.
explanation: A specific, known door is meant, so the definite article is required: 'open the door'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: When I was in 5th grade, / I use to / ride on my / red bicycle.
explanation: A past habit is expressed by 'used to', not 'use to'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. There was a saying that they’re their own enemies with negligble reason to be shared.
explanation: 'Negligble' is a misspelling; the correct spelling is 'negligible'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Would you / like to / watch an movie / tonight at eight?
explanation: 'Movie' begins with a consonant sound, so the article must be 'a movie', not 'an movie'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. This region was struck by unusual wave of violence last year.
explanation: The singular countable noun phrase needs an indefinite article: 'struck by an unusual wave of violence'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The lower strata are mostly not benifitted by the reign of monarchy.
explanation: The word is misspelt; the correct spelling is 'benefited' (or 'benefitted'), not 'benifitted'. The rest, including the plural 'strata are', is correct.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The news is very good to be true.
explanation: The idiomatic structure is 'too + adjective + to + verb', so it must be 'too good to be true'; 'very' cannot be used with the 'to-infinitive' of excess.

prompt: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: I need to buy an new iPhone.
The cat sat on the windowsill
She is the best singer in the choir.
He is an artist who paints landscapes.
explanation: 'New' begins with a consonant sound /nj/, so the article must be 'a new iPhone', not 'an new iPhone'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error mark 'No error' as your answer.
sentence: The aeroplane took down / without the passengers after / making a sudden announcement.
explanation: An aeroplane 'takes off', not 'takes down'; the phrasal verb is wrong.

prompt: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.
sentence: Raveena’s daughter Kavya is most intelligent student and she consistently achieves top grades.
explanation: 'Most intelligent student' needs 'the' for the superlative; since the sentence merely praises her, the correct rectification is 'an intelligent student'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, select ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: It was possible to achieve anything, / if one has the grit and determination / to keep going.
options: It was possible to achieve anything
if one has the grit and determination
explanation: The 'if' clause is in the present ('has'), so the main clause must also be present: 'It is possible to achieve anything'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error mark 'No error' as your answer.
sentence: Father took the newspaper / in his hand to / go through it once again.
explanation: The sentence is correct: past tense 'took', the phrase 'in his hand', and the infinitive of purpose 'to go through it' are all properly used.

prompt: The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’.
sentence: The judges eliminated the / classical singer, as she dropped of / in the middle of the competition.
options: in the middle of the competition.
classical singer, as she dropped of
explanation: The correct phrasal verb is 'dropped out' (withdrew), not 'dropped of'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
sentence: The project was completed / more quicker / than expected.
explanation: 'Quicker' is already comparative, so adding 'more' creates a double comparative; it should be 'more quickly' or simply 'quicker'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Mrs. Meera and family / received his letter / a week ago.
explanation: The pronoun must agree with the subject 'Mrs. Meera and family', so it should be 'her letter', not 'his letter'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Urgent activities are those things / that you must do immediately, / as they require quick action / and cannot be put on.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb for postponing is 'put off', not 'put on'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into three segments. One of them may contain an adverbial usage error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If you don’t find any error, select ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Mr. Narayanan / is a rather / lazy man.
explanation: 'Is a rather lazy man' is correct usage; 'rather' properly modifies the adjective 'lazy' after the article.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: In geography class, / the teacher told the students, / "Switzerland lies / inside Germany, France, Austria, and Italy."
options: inside Germany, France, Austria, and Italy.
explanation: Switzerland lies 'between' (not 'inside') the four named countries, as clearly separate places are being referred to.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into three segments. One of them may contain an adverbial usage error. Select the option that has the segment with the error. If you don’t find any error, select ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Mrs. Arunima / speaks / Telugu well.
explanation: The sentence is correct: the adverb 'well' properly follows the object 'Telugu' after the verb 'speaks'.

prompt: The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’.
sentence: The meeting was called off / due to a medical emergency of / the manager of the company.
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct; 'was called off' and 'due to a medical emergency of the manager' are both acceptable.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Ramya is working / hardly / to get good marks.
explanation: 'Hardly' means 'almost not'; the intended sense of diligent effort requires the adverb 'hard' — 'working hard'.

prompt: The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’.
sentence: The volunteer gave on to / the food packets to the / children of the orphanage.
explanation: 'Gave on to' is not a valid phrasal verb here; it should be 'gave away' or 'gave out' the food packets.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: I goes to / attend dance classes at / the National Dance Academy.
explanation: The first-person subject 'I' takes the base verb, so it must be 'I go to', not 'I goes to'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Since the little girl answers / a few simple questions, / her parents say that / she is too intelligent.
explanation: 'Too' implies excess with a negative result; praising the girl requires 'very intelligent'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: In order to connect / these themes to a wider / historical context, Rahul go / beyond aesthetic analysis.
explanation: The singular proper-noun subject 'Rahul' needs the singular verb 'goes', not 'go'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The manager asked / the cooking team, “Who / among you is to baked the / Christmas cake this year?”
options: among you is to baked the
explanation: After 'is to', the bare infinitive is required, so 'is to baked' must be 'is to bake'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: How long are you working / for your current employer / and why don’t you / look for better opportunities?
explanation: 'How long' with an action continuing up to now requires the present perfect continuous: 'How long have you been working'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: That day we reached late for the competition and even though the competition went on smooth, I felt bad about Shivani losing it.
explanation: The verb 'went on' needs the adverb 'smoothly', not the adjective 'smooth'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: According to the encyclopaedia, a oasis is an area which is made fertile by a source of freshwater.
explanation: 'Oasis' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an oasis'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The workers called out / the strike because / the management acceded to / all their demands.
explanation: Since the management met the demands, the workers would 'call off' (cancel) the strike, not 'call out'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Passengers started behaving / violent when / they were asked / to leave the bus station.
explanation: 'Behaving' needs the adverb 'violently' to describe the manner of the action.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The companies were / giving in the prizes / to attract customers / during the festive season.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb is 'giving away the prizes'; 'giving in' means to surrender.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: Ramayana is an ancient Sanskrit epic; it is believed to be written around 500 BC to 100 BC.
explanation: Names of epics and sacred books take the definite article: 'The Ramayana is an ancient...'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: His mother’s transfer from a small town to Delhi brought up a huge change in his schooling.
options: from a small town to Delhi
explanation: The idiom meaning 'to cause' is 'brought about a huge change', not 'brought up'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: This artwork / are a wonderful example / of the period's vogue / for realistic style.
explanation: The singular subject 'This artwork' requires the singular verb 'is a wonderful example'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I noticed that they / did not went to / the museum but entered / a shopping complex.
explanation: After the auxiliary 'did not', the base form is used: 'did not go'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. It was noticed / that he truthful / answered the questions / raised by the Headmistress.
explanation: The verb 'answered' needs the adverb 'truthfully' instead of the adjective 'truthful'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: There are eight planets in our solar system and a Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
options: and a Earth is the third
explanation: Unique proper nouns like Earth take 'the', so it should be 'and the Earth is the third'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: ‘You expressed your opinion/ very clearly /but I am sorry/ I cannot agree to you’.
explanation: One agrees 'with' a person and 'to' a proposal, so it must be 'I cannot agree with you'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: We has travelled / to many states / of India to get / an essence of its diversity.
explanation: The plural subject 'We' takes 'have travelled', not 'has travelled'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The manager noticed / that Pragya / was first to reach / the office on Saturday.
explanation: Ordinals take the definite article: 'was the first to reach'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: A owl is a bird which has wide eyes, asymmetrical ears and is found mostly in forests.
options: and is found mostly in forests.
explanation: 'Owl' starts with a vowel sound, so the correct article is 'An owl'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Everyone have/ to join health orientation/ classes before/ going for trekking.
explanation: 'Everyone' is a singular indefinite pronoun and takes 'has to join'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I used to eat into / in the evening / when my parents / were on night shifts.
explanation: The intended phrasal verb is 'eat out' (eat away from home); 'eat into' means to erode or consume.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The soldiers / were selected / on the section / of ‘gallantry of spirits’.
explanation: The idiomatic phrase is 'on the basis of', not 'on the section of'; 'section' is the wrong noun in this fixed prepositional phrase.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The teacher will never / give you punishment / if you will / come on time.
explanation: In a conditional clause of Type 1, the 'if' clause takes the simple present, not 'will'; it should be 'if you come on time'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: There was an gang of thieves spotted at our local bank, make sure to be careful.
explanation: 'Gang' begins with a consonant sound, so it takes 'a', not 'an' — 'There was a gang'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: Policeman came to my village and asked about a person who burgled a house last night.
explanation: A singular countable noun used for the first time needs an indefinite article: 'A policeman came to my village'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I am very much / obliged of my friend / for the help / he rendered to me.
explanation: 'Obliged' takes the preposition 'to' when referring to a person: 'obliged to my friend'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: There’s an quiet street down the left that you can use for your dance practice.
explanation: 'Quiet' begins with a consonant sound, so the article must be 'a': 'There's a quiet street'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: Geeta was working now but she can be seen swimming in the river every evening.
explanation: The time marker 'now' requires the present continuous, so 'was working' must be 'is working'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My Vice-Chancellor works / eighteen hours / a day, / seven days week.
explanation: The distributive expression needs the article 'a': 'seven days a week', parallel to 'eighteen hours a day'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Since childhood, Monty / ate his food / fast and he / will not change.
explanation: 'Since childhood' indicates an action continuing from a past point, so the present perfect is required: 'has eaten his food'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: Today she said to her friend, “You’re the sweetest person I have met ever”.
explanation: With the present perfect, 'ever' is placed before the past participle: 'I have ever met'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: The chief guest gave out prizes to the meritorious students of the school.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb for distributing prizes is 'gave away prizes'; 'gave out' is not the idiomatic collocation here.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The couple / preferred to walk / until the last house / of the town.
explanation: 'Until' refers only to time; for distance or place, 'up to the last house' is required.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Hard had she / thrown the basketball / when it fell / on the ground.
explanation: The correlative structure is 'Hardly had + subject + V3 ... when', so 'Hard had she' must be 'Hardly had she'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: During winters, most of the trains are not running on time in North India.
explanation: Names of seasons are used in the singular in such expressions: 'During winter'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in the usage of
sentence: indefinite articles. We took / an ice / and applied it on / the wound.
explanation: 'Ice' is an uncountable noun and cannot take the indefinite article; it should be 'some ice' (or 'an ice cube').

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She was singing / beautifully in / the concert hall / last night.
explanation: The definite past time marker 'last night' calls for the simple past, so 'She was singing' should be 'She sang'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Rashmi was / quite amusing when / she heard about / what had happened.
explanation: A person experiencing the feeling takes the past participle form: 'quite amused', since '-ing' participles describe the cause.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: After a while, / she look up / and saw that / it was getting dark.
explanation: The narrative is in the past tense, so the verb must be 'looked up', not 'look up'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I am going / to buy a red car / with a leather seats / and a sunroof.
explanation: The indefinite article 'a' cannot precede a plural noun; it should be 'with leather seats'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: After your insistence, / my sister / checked / a mailbox again.
explanation: A specific, previously known mailbox requires the definite article: 'checked the mailbox again'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Our plane / arrived at / the Mumbai airport / at the right time.
explanation: Names of airports are proper nouns and take no article, so it should be 'Mumbai airport', not 'the Mumbai airport'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Mathematics help/ in developing/ the logical mindset /of students.
explanation: 'Mathematics' ends in -s but is a singular subject, so the verb must be 'helps'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: It is his job / to chase out / clients with / outstanding debts.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb for pursuing debtors is 'chase up', not 'chase out'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: If she exercises daily, / she would / remain energetic / and fit forever.
explanation: A Type-1 conditional with 'If + present simple' requires 'will' in the main clause: 'she will remain'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He have / workers from / Ireland and France / in his factory.
explanation: The singular subject 'He' takes 'has', not 'have'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The teacher will / certainly help you / if you will / ask her.
explanation: In a conditional 'if' clause we use the simple present, not 'will': 'if you ask her'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: In this cold weather, / there’s nothing / like good / cup of coffee.
explanation: The singular countable noun phrase needs an article: 'like a good cup of coffee'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: They have decided / to wind out / their business / without delay.
explanation: The idiom meaning to close a business is 'wind up', not 'wind out'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: I had seen / her with her mother / in the cinema hall / yesterday.
explanation: 'Yesterday' marks a completed past action, so simple past 'I saw' is required, not past perfect.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: (1) Ganga was (2) out shopping at the mall (3) and ran over (4) her schoolmate.
explanation: 'Ran over' means to hit with a vehicle; the sense of meeting by chance requires 'ran into her schoolmate'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The hotel room, / which we / booked, / isn’t enough big.
explanation: 'Enough' follows the adjective it modifies, so the correct form is 'isn't big enough'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: Mumbai is the city of dreams but it is a expensive city too.
explanation: 'Expensive' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an expensive city'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.
sentence: Pratigya arrived / to the / railway station / five hours early.
explanation: 'Arrive' takes 'at' with a specific place: 'arrived at the railway station'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The meeting / will taking / place next / Wednesday.
explanation: After the modal 'will' the bare infinitive is used: 'will take place'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: (1) When Christy (2) grew out, (3) he turned out (4) to be a gentleman.
explanation: The phrasal verb for reaching adulthood is 'grew up', not 'grew out'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She / did not watched / Frankenstein / last night.
explanation: After the auxiliary 'did' the base form is required: 'did not watch'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.
sentence: (A) I am hearing / (B) that the heat wave / (C) is going to be / (D) worse this year.
explanation: 'Hear' is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous form; it should be 'I hear that...'.

prompt: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: When it / come to football, / my brother is / an addict.
explanation: The singular subject 'it' requires 'comes': 'When it comes to football'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Don’t go / outside / because it is / raining heavy.
explanation: The verb 'raining' needs an adverb, not an adjective, so 'raining heavy' must be 'raining heavily'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Throw of / the old shoes; / nobody will wear / them now.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb is 'throw away/out'; 'throw of' is not a valid combination.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: She was fond of walking along the path besides the lake.
explanation: 'Beside' means 'by the side of', while 'besides' means 'in addition to'; the path runs by the side of the lake, so 'beside the lake' is required.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The shop / usually opened / ten minutes / late.
explanation: The adverb 'usually' indicates a habitual action, so the simple present 'opens' is needed instead of the past 'opened'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: When Serena / will arrive, / she will / call you.
explanation: A time clause introduced by 'when' takes the simple present, not 'will'; it should be 'When Serena arrives'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.
sentence: (A) It is sad / (B) that you / (C) are believing / (D) in superstitious rituals.
explanation: 'Believe' is a stative verb and takes no continuous form, so 'are believing' must be 'believe'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: If it will rain tomorrow, I will stay at home.
explanation: In a first conditional, the if-clause takes the simple present, so 'If it will rain' should be 'If it rains'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Shall have / you bring / your note-book / tomorrow?
explanation: A simple future question needs 'Will you bring...?'; 'Shall have you bring' is not a valid auxiliary structure.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Are today / a working day / or a / holiday?
explanation: 'Today' is a singular subject here, so the verb must be 'Is today a working day...?'

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The new / secretary / does not likes / me.
explanation: After the auxiliary 'does', the base form of the verb is used, so 'does not likes' must be 'does not like'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: Emily is a American living in Paris for her work.
explanation: 'American' begins with a vowel sound, so the article must be 'an American'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.
sentence: This is / a doll / and there is / a umbrella.
explanation: 'Umbrella' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an umbrella'.

prompt: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
sentence: I will be study around 7 o’clock.
explanation: 'Will be' must be followed by the present participle, so 'be study' should be 'be studying'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option 'No error'.
sentence: All of us were a little nervous when we came into this room today.
options: when we came into this room today
explanation: The sentence is correct: the past tense with 'today', 'a little nervous', and 'came into' (movement) are all grammatically acceptable.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option 'No error'.
sentence: When he goes on a business trip, he is usually taking his wife.
options: he is usually taking his wife
explanation: 'Usually' signals a habitual action, so the simple present 'he usually takes his wife' is required, not the continuous.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option 'No error'.
sentence: The sun rises at 6.35 yesterday morning.
explanation: The past time marker 'yesterday morning' demands the simple past, so 'rises' must be 'rose'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option 'No error'.
sentence: Sh! Someone listens to our conversation.
explanation: The action is happening at the moment of speaking, so the present continuous 'is listening to' is needed.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. Rice of a best quality is available in the nearby supermarket at eighty rupees per kilo.
explanation: A superlative adjective takes the definite article, so 'a best quality' must be 'the best quality'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option 'No error'.
sentence: I am hearing a strange noise now.
explanation: 'Hear' is a stative verb of perception and is not used in the continuous form; it should be 'I hear a strange noise now.'

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Two elderly ladies narrated an rather improbable story to the police.
explanation: The article depends on the sound of the following word 'rather', which begins with a consonant sound, so 'a rather improbable story' is correct.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I had to hold on to the wall to steady itself or I could have fallen.
explanation: The reflexive pronoun must agree with the subject 'I', so it should be 'to steady myself'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I remember a friend to me buying several pairs of shoes at a sale.
explanation: The double possessive form is required: 'a friend of mine', not 'a friend to me'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The bottle slipped with my hand and broke into a thousand pieces.
explanation: The fixed combination is 'slip from', indicating separation, so it should be 'slipped from my hand'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He wondered what was the reason for her refusal to accompany him.
explanation: In an indirect/embedded question the normal subject-verb order is kept: 'what the reason was', without inversion.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She picked up the books lie on the table and put them on the shelf.
explanation: A present participle is needed to modify 'books', so it should be 'the books lying on the table'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Miss Marple is neither a good singer or the good stage artist.
explanation: 'Neither' must be paired with 'nor', and the parallel structure needs 'nor a good stage artist'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Our new secretary’s performance have been quite impressive.
explanation: The singular subject 'performance' requires the singular verb 'has been'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: There will probably be a lot of fish in their nets, will there?
explanation: A positive statement takes a negative question tag, so it should be 'won't there?'

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: One of the proposals received by us seem very interesting.
explanation: 'One of + plural noun' takes a singular verb, so it should be 'seems very interesting'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: You cannot lead a healthy life although you stop smoking.
explanation: The sense is a negative condition, so 'unless you stop smoking' is required instead of 'although'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The information you are asking for is quite irrelevance.
explanation: After the linking verb 'is' an adjective is needed, so it should be 'quite irrelevant', not the noun 'irrelevance'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Anybody who does not stop at the red light will fined.
explanation: The passive construction requires 'will be fined' after the modal 'will'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She will come to work though it doesn’t rain tomorrow.
explanation: The intended concessive-conditional meaning needs 'even if it rains tomorrow'; 'though it doesn't rain' contradicts the sense.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Either Ramesh or Reema have the keys to the cupboard.
explanation: With 'either ... or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'Reema', so 'has' is correct.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The two trains gave the illusion of been stationary.
explanation: After the preposition 'of' a gerund is required: 'of being stationary'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Sam took a little time to thought before he replied.
explanation: An infinitive takes the base form of the verb, so it should be 'to think'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He is over eighty and dare not read without glasses.
explanation: With the third-person singular subject 'He' in this affirmative-clause structure, the verb should be 'dares not read'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The jury are from different parts of the country.
explanation: The collective noun 'jury' is treated as one body here and takes the singular verb 'is from'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Nobody has ever listened to me so attentive.
explanation: An adverb, not an adjective, must modify the verb 'listened', so 'so attentive' should be 'so attentively'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She has been working tirelessly since hours.
explanation: 'Since' marks a point of time while 'for' marks a duration; 'hours' is a period, so it should be 'for hours'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I was sorry to be hearing of his misfortune.
explanation: After 'sorry' a simple infinitive is used: 'sorry to hear', not the continuous 'to be hearing'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Do you earn so much to make both ends meet?
explanation: To express sufficiency the structure is 'enough to', so 'so much to make both ends meet' should be 'enough to make both ends meet'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Once upon a time, / a beautiful princess / has fallen in love / with a poor farmer.
explanation: 'Once upon a time' indicates a finished past action, so the simple past 'fell in love' is required instead of the present perfect 'has fallen'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Her health has being / steadily improving / since she started / practising yoga.
explanation: The present perfect continuous needs the past participle 'been', so 'has being' must be 'has been'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The news / of his involvement / in illegal activities / have shocked everybody.
explanation: 'News' ends in -s but is a singular uncountable noun, so it takes 'has shocked'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My neighbour is / an young businessman / who is very friendly / with everyone.
explanation: 'Young' begins with the consonant sound /j/, so the article must be 'a young businessman'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The farmers are using / HYV seeds / so then they can get / a better yield.
explanation: A clause of purpose requires the conjunction 'so that', not 'so then'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I saw several / French colonial villas / within my visit / to Puducherry.
explanation: 'Within' cannot express time throughout an event; the correct preposition is 'during my visit'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: No sooner / did the chairman arrived / than the / proceedings commenced.
explanation: In the inverted 'No sooner' structure the auxiliary 'did' takes the base verb, so it should be 'did the chairman arrive'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Please switch off / all the lights / before you / are leaving the room.
explanation: A clause introduced by 'before' takes the simple present, not the present continuous: 'before you leave the room'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He wanted to know / the reason / why his low score / in Mathematics.
explanation: 'Why' must introduce a clause with a finite verb; with only a noun phrase the correct form is 'for his low score'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: As soon he heard / the sound of thunder, / he hid / under the bed.
explanation: The correlative is 'as soon as', so 'As soon he heard' must be 'As soon as he heard'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She speaks / very highly / of both her / daughter-in-laws.
explanation: In compound nouns of this type the principal word is pluralised, giving 'daughters-in-law'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He could not / get a job / despite of / his best efforts.
explanation: 'Despite' is already a preposition and takes no 'of'; only 'in spite of' uses it.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: You need / to sign / these important documents / by ink.
explanation: The idiomatic preposition for writing materials is 'in': 'sign in ink', not 'by ink'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I asked Dhruv / when he has plan / to settle / the dues.
explanation: After the past reporting verb 'asked', the tense must shift back: 'when he had planned' / 'when he had plans'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: This is / only mistake / he has made / in the dictation.
explanation: The definite article is compulsory before 'only' used as a limiting adjective: 'the only mistake'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Much of us / lack the / important virtue / of patience.
explanation: 'Us' refers to countable persons, so the quantifier must be 'Many of us', not 'Much of us'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He is / too immature / for handle / the situation.
explanation: The structure 'too + adjective' is followed by an infinitive, so 'for handle' must be 'to handle'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: His loyalty / and honesty / are above / suspect.
explanation: The idiom requires the noun 'suspicion' ('above suspicion'); 'suspect' is a verb/adjective and is wrong here.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Parul is / ten years / elder than / her sibling.
explanation: 'Elder' is never followed by 'than'; the correct comparative with 'than' is 'older than'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He is / afraid from / all insects / that crawl.
explanation: The fixed combination is 'afraid of', not 'afraid from'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Everyone was surprised / at his indefatigable courage and determination / to achieve what he desired.
options: At his indefatigable courage and determination
explanation: 'Surprised at' is the correct preposition and the rest of the sentence is idiomatic and grammatical, so there is no error.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: As is usual with stories of this genre, / in spite of their varying socio political realities, / the youngsters have fallen in love / with each other madly.
options: the youngsters have fallen in love
in spite of their varying socio political realities
As is usual with stories of this genre
explanation: The adverb belongs with the verb phrase: 'have fallen madly in love with each other', not 'with each other madly'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Psychology has been / defined the scientific study of / human psyche and behaviour.
explanation: 'Define' in the passive needs 'as' before the complement: 'has been defined as the scientific study of'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Fortunately, he passed the exams / with dint of / sheer hard work and diligence.
explanation: The fixed idiom is 'by dint of', not 'with dint of'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: The research fellow defended / his thesis scholarly / and obtained the degree.
explanation: 'Scholarly' is an adjective and cannot modify the verb 'defended'; use 'in a scholarly manner'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: He took a hurried glance / on the newspaper / and swiftly left for work.
explanation: One takes a glance 'at' something, so 'on the newspaper' should be 'at the newspaper'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
