explanation: After 'the' a noun is needed, so the adjective 'meaningless' must become the noun 'meaninglessness'.

prompt: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.
sentence: This is the eldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
options: This is the more older standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the most old standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the more elder standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the oldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
explanation: 'Eldest' is used only for family members; for age of a structure the correct superlative is 'oldest'.

prompt: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.
sentence: The boy told his mother that he saw the most tall giraffe at the zoo.
options: The boy told his mother that he saw the tallest giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the most taller giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the most tallest giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the more taller giraffe at the zoo.
explanation: 'Tall' is a one-syllable adjective, so its superlative is 'tallest', not 'most tall' or 'most tallest'.

prompt: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.
sentence: Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the bad.
options: Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the worst.
Earlier, he was feeling good, but things took a turn for the bad.
Earlier, he was feeling well, but things took a turn for the ill.
Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the ill.
explanation: The idiom is 'take a turn for the worst/worse'; 'for the bad' is not idiomatic English.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: A night alone / in a hotel / can be lonely prospect.
explanation: The singular countable noun 'prospect' needs an indefinite article: 'can be a lonely prospect'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Why don’t / you throw this / paper on the dust bin?
explanation: Movement towards the inside of something takes 'into', so it should be 'throw this paper into the dustbin'.

prompt: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The
sentence: underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The new restaurant on Main Street is cheap than the old one.
explanation: A comparison with 'than' requires the comparative degree, so 'is cheap than' must become 'is cheaper than'.

prompt: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.
sentence: He is the better-looking hero in the entire film industry.
options: He is the best-looking hero in the entire film industry.
He is the good-looking hero than the entire film industry.
He is the best-looking hero more than the entire film industry.
He is the good-looking hero in the entire film industry.
explanation: Comparing one hero with all others in the entire industry requires the superlative degree, 'the best-looking'.

prompt: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The
sentence: underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. This car is lesser expensive than the one I had come to buy.
explanation: Before an adjective in a comparison the correct form is 'less expensive', not 'lesser expensive'; 'lesser' is not used with adjectives.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. For an all-too-brief period between the late 1980s and the late 2000s, a world was characterised by convergence.
explanation: 'World' is a unique noun, so it takes the definite article: 'the world was characterised by convergence'.

prompt: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The
sentence: underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. He is good at playing the guitar than his brother.
explanation: The presence of 'than' demands the comparative form, so 'is good at' becomes 'is better at'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. We think of the past history of the world as fixed but of the future as undecided and open to a wealth off possibilities.
explanation: The fixed phrase is 'a wealth of possibilities'; 'off' is an incorrect preposition here.

prompt: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The
sentence: underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The weather is cold tonight than it was yesterday.
explanation: 'Than' requires the comparative degree: 'The weather is colder tonight than it was yesterday'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. A soothe voice must convey both confidence and intimacy, qualities which can be attributed to a few key components.
explanation: An adjective is needed before 'voice', so the present participle 'soothing' must replace the verb 'soothe'.

prompt: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The
sentence: underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. Sohan is the older brother of my best friend.
explanation: For seniority within a family relationship, 'elder' is used attributively rather than 'older'.

prompt: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.
sentence: He was carefullest while stealing the crown jewels.
options: He was more careful while stealing the crown jewels.
He was most carefuller while stealing the crown jewels.
He was carefuller while stealing the crown jewels.
He was most careful while stealing the crown jewels.
explanation: Adjectives of three or more syllables form the superlative with 'most', giving 'most careful' instead of 'carefullest'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: It is commonly believed / that Democracy is / the best form / of the government.
explanation: 'Government' here is used in a general, abstract sense, so no article is used: 'the best form of government'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Manisha saw an old elephant / in the wildlife reserve / while she was / on safari tour.
explanation: The countable singular noun phrase needs an indefinite article: 'on a safari tour'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My daughter was / invited to lunch / hosted by the Governor / at his residence.
explanation: Because the meal is specified by 'hosted by the Governor', a countable use with the article is required: 'invited to a lunch'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Henry is known / as an excellent writer / and good communicator / in English.
explanation: Two distinct roles are described, so each noun needs its own article: 'and a good communicator'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: My father told me / that in his childhood / he was walking / to school every day.
explanation: A repeated past habit signalled by 'every day' takes the simple past or 'used to', so 'he was walking' should be 'he walked'/'he used to walk'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Guard over / making mistakes / by carefully checking / the assigned task.
explanation: The verb collocates with 'against' when warning of something undesirable: 'Guard against making mistakes'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: If he had paid / attention to the announcement, / he had not / missed the train.
explanation: In a third conditional, the 'if had + V3' clause is matched by 'would not have + V3', so 'he had not missed' must be 'he would not have missed'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: The team played / really well, but / they lose the game / in the final minutes.
explanation: The sentence is in the past tense ('played'), so the coordinated verb must also be past: 'they lost the game'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: They decided to / travel in train / instead of driving / to New Delhi.
explanation: Means of transport takes 'by', so 'travel in train' should be 'travel by train'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. They had two bedrooms among them, one for the girls and one for the boys.
explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two; for the two people implied here 'between them' is correct.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: They had been dancing / for an hour / when our dance teacher / had arrived.
explanation: With 'when' marking the later action, the past perfect is wrong; it should be the simple past 'arrived' since 'had been dancing' already shows the earlier action.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I want to / give you / an information about / the missing necklace.
explanation: 'Information' is an uncountable noun and cannot take the article 'an'; correct form is 'some information about' or just 'information about'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She performed / the dance routine / perfect, / impressing everyone.
explanation: The word modifies the verb 'performed', so the adverb 'perfectly' is required, not the adjective 'perfect'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: She was writing / a letter to her grandmother / when the power / gone out.
explanation: A past-tense clause needs the second form of the verb, so 'gone out' must be 'went out' (past participle cannot stand without an auxiliary).

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My younger daughter, / Kanu prefer / dark chocolate / to yoghurt.
explanation: The singular proper-noun subject 'Kanu' needs the singular verb 'prefers'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The new software / consists from / several features / and tools.
explanation: The verb 'consist' takes the fixed preposition 'of', so it should be 'consists of several features'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: In America, / most of the people / can speak / the English well.
explanation: Names of languages take no article in the general sense; it should be 'speak English well'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. To much seriousness hardens the world, pinning it down with rules.
explanation: Before the quantifier 'much' + noun, the intensifier is 'too much', not 'to much'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. All these things happen/ because she do not / pay heed to my words.
explanation: The third-person singular subject 'she' requires 'does not', not 'do not'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She is very good / in playing / the guitar / and singing songs.
explanation: 'Good' collocates with 'at' before a gerund, so it should be 'good at playing'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: This scripture / has been /translated in / seventy languages.
explanation: 'Translate' takes 'into' when showing the target language: 'translated into seventy languages'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Mohan is respected / by everyone / because he works / hardly.
explanation: 'Hardly' means 'scarcely'; the intended sense 'with effort' requires the adverb 'hard'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: The school shall reopened / after summer / vacations of / one month.
explanation: A modal like 'shall' must be followed by the bare infinitive, so 'shall reopened' should be 'shall reopen'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Harish told me / in the morning / that Gaurav will / come tomorrow.
explanation: After the past reporting verb 'told', the reported clause shifts to 'would', giving 'that Gaurav would come'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Radha will have learnt cooking by the time she will have married.
explanation: After 'by the time' referring to the future, the clause takes the simple present/present perfect: 'she gets married' or 'she has married'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Mr Sharma would have left / the station / by this time / tomorrow.
explanation: 'By this time tomorrow' points to future time, so the verb should be the future perfect 'will have left', not 'would have left'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Harish says / that his sister / loves to play / harmonium.
explanation: Names of musical instruments after 'play' take the definite article: 'play the harmonium'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. A old woman suddenly laughed, sounding just like an amused hen.
explanation: 'Old' begins with a vowel sound, so the article must be 'An old woman'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. As soon as I shall win the lottery, I hope to buy a Ferrari.
explanation: A clause introduced by 'as soon as' takes the simple present for future reference, so 'shall win' should be 'win'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The little child / wrote his name / quick / on the wall.
explanation: The verb 'wrote' must be modified by the adverb 'quickly', not the adjective 'quick'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: This is the first time / I ate such / a tasty cake.
explanation: After 'This is the first time', the present perfect is required: 'I have eaten such a tasty cake.'

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. My teacher told me that / all that / glitters was not gold.
explanation: The proverb states a universal truth, so the simple present is retained: 'all that glitters is not gold.'

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: A music / is a great way / to express / your emotions.
explanation: 'Music' is an uncountable noun used in a general sense, so it takes no article: 'Music is a great way...'

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. He told me / that he goes / to the market / to buy a laptop.
explanation: In reported speech after the past-tense 'told', the verb must be back-shifted: 'that he was going / he went'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Shelley and Keats are great writers, but I prefer the last.
explanation: When only two persons are compared, 'the latter' (not 'the last') is correct.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I will celebrating New Year at my old residence as usual.
options: at my old residence as usual.
explanation: 'Will' must be followed by the base form: 'will celebrate' (or 'will be celebrating').

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Please / explain me / how this plan / did not work.
explanation: 'Explain' cannot take a direct indirect object; it needs the preposition 'to': 'explain to me'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. When I bought the book, I thought it will be interesting.
explanation: With the past-tense main verb 'thought', the future must shift to 'would be interesting'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Some / private banks / pay their employees / good.
explanation: The action verb 'pay' needs the adverb 'well', not the adjective 'good'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. What most off us want most is to move forward.
explanation: The preposition 'of' is required, not the adverb 'off': 'most of us'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The ball / I kicked / went highly / in the sky.
explanation: 'High' denotes physical height; 'highly' means 'to a great degree', so it should be 'went high'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. In Nepal, the food is more cheaper than in Sri Lanka.
explanation: 'Cheaper' is already comparative, so 'more cheaper' is a double comparative; use 'cheaper'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I will going on an official tour next week.
explanation: 'Will' takes the base form: 'will go' (or 'will be going').

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Jaya said that she will become topper in her class.
explanation: After the reporting verb 'said', 'will' becomes 'would': 'she would become the topper'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. If he will come early, we will leave on time.
explanation: In a first conditional, the if-clause takes the simple present: 'If he comes early'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. My relatives shall have reached Amritsar by now.
explanation: With the third person, simple futurity requires 'will', not 'shall': 'will have reached'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. They will start their journey after the breakfast.
explanation: Names of meals used in a general sense take no article: 'after breakfast'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Ishita will playing Tennis for her favourite team.
explanation: 'Will' must be followed by the base verb: 'will play' (or 'will be playing').

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I had / a bad habit of / waking up / lately.
explanation: 'Lately' means 'recently'; the intended sense of time is 'late', so it should be 'waking up late'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Perhaps my family visit the Taj Mahal next month.
explanation: 'Next month' signals future time, so the verb must be 'will visit'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: I have seen / a movie / on schooling / yesterday.
explanation: 'Yesterday' denotes a finished past time, so the present perfect 'have seen' is wrong; it must be the simple past 'saw'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. You shall repented tomorrow for your misdeeds.
explanation: After the modal 'shall', the base form of the verb is required, so 'shall repented' must be 'shall repent'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Did / her friend / went to / school yesterday?
explanation: After the auxiliary 'did', the first form of the verb is used, so 'went' should be 'go'.

prompt: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: The Mona Lisa is a famous painting by Leonardo da Vinci.
She is the only person who can speak five languages fluently.
He is a doctor who specialises in the treating rare diseases.
I saw the movie that won the Academy Award for Best Picture.
explanation: A gerund after a preposition takes no article, so 'in the treating rare diseases' should be 'in treating rare diseases'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Tushar is junior than all his colleagues.
explanation: Latin comparatives such as junior, senior, superior and inferior take 'to', not 'than': 'junior to all his colleagues'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The boy whose the sister is ill has left.
explanation: The relative pronoun 'whose' already shows possession, so no article follows it; it should be 'whose sister'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. If you work hard, you secure good marks.
explanation: In a first (probable) conditional, the if-clause is present simple and the main clause takes 'will', so 'you secure' should be 'you will secure'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: She has / bought / a car / two years ago.
explanation: 'Two years ago' fixes a definite past time, which is incompatible with the present perfect; 'She has bought' should be 'She bought'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Tuntun and her friends dance beautiful.
explanation: The action verb 'dance' needs an adverb, not an adjective, so 'beautiful' should be 'beautifully'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. When Nisha will have finished her task?
explanation: In a wh-question the auxiliary comes before the subject, so 'When Nisha will' should be 'When will Nisha'.

prompt: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: I saw a movie that was directed by Steven Spielberg.
She is the only person who can solve this difficult math problem.
He is an lawyer who works for a prestigious law firm.
The Great Wall of China is a popular tourist attraction.
explanation: 'Lawyer' begins with a consonant sound, so it takes 'a', not 'an': 'a lawyer'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The cholera is a frightful disease.
explanation: Names of diseases are used without 'the' in a general sense, so 'The cholera' should be 'Cholera'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Vikram is very stronger than I am.
explanation: 'Very' cannot modify a comparative adjective; 'much stronger' (or 'far stronger') is required.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I shall be playing for four hours.
explanation: With a completed duration up to a future point, the future perfect continuous is needed: 'I shall have been playing for four hours.'

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. They have less books than I have.
explanation: 'Books' is a countable noun, so the quantifier must be 'fewer', not 'less'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The platinum is a precious metal.
explanation: Material/uncountable nouns used generally take no article, so 'The platinum' should be 'Platinum'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Sanjana rubbed her eyes hardly.
explanation: 'Hardly' means 'scarcely'; the adverb of manner meaning 'forcefully' is 'hard', so it should be 'rubbed her eyes hard'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The blue is a beautiful colour.
explanation: Names of colours used in a general sense take no article, so 'The blue' should be 'Blue'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Ravi will go to the England.
explanation: Names of countries like England do not take 'the', so it should be 'go to England'.

prompt: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: I love the taste of fresh strawberries in the summer.
She is the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize.
He is chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.
The Earth revolves around the Sun.
explanation: A singular countable noun naming a profession needs an article: 'He is a chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.'

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The new/ smartphone is/absolutely best than/ the latest model.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: The recommendations of the committee / regarding changes in the eligibility criteria / was not accept.
options: regarding changes in the eligibility criteria
explanation: The plural subject 'recommendations' needs a plural verb and the passive requires the past participle: 'were not accepted'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: My mother is 51 years old, / and my uncle is 48 years old. / So my mother is old than my uncle.
options: and my uncle is 48 years old.
So my mother is old than my uncle.
explanation: With 'than' the comparative form is required, so 'old than my uncle' should be 'older than my uncle'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Chetan's room is clean / than Ram's room because / Chetan cleans it more often than Ram.
options: Chetan cleans it more often than Ram
explanation: The comparison with 'than' demands the comparative degree: 'Chetan's room is cleaner'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: The students were diligently / studying for their exams / for weeks before you arrived.
explanation: An action continuing over 'weeks before you arrived' needs the past perfect continuous: 'The students had been diligently studying'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: There is only one way / to have a happier marred life / and I will learn it soon.
options: to have a happier marred life
and I will learn it soon.
explanation: 'Marred' (spoiled) is the wrong word here; the intended word is 'married', so it should be 'a happier married life'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Spanish person are well known worldwide / for their warm hospitality / and food.
options: Spanish person are well known worldwide
explanation: The plural verb 'are' needs a plural subject, so 'Spanish person' should be 'Spanish people' (or 'Spaniards').

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.
sentence: After months of / meticulous planning and hard work, / a team successfully launched / their innovative product to the market.
options: their innovative product to the market.
explanation: A specific, already-identified team requires the definite article: 'the team successfully launched'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: My friend, / Priya looks more cheerful today / as she celebrates her birthday.
explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct: 'looks more cheerful' is a valid comparative after a linking verb and the tense sequence is consistent.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Her decision, / given the complex circumstances, / was too impulsively made.
explanation: After the linking verb 'was' an adjective is needed, and 'too' requires a completing clause, so it should be 'was very impulsive'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

and has decided to take action.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Tara has been playing / cricket with her friends / since noon.
explanation: 'Since noon' marks a point of time and correctly takes the present perfect continuous 'has been playing', so there is no error.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: I thought of this idea / just when you called / me yesterday.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My brother trains young girls at the football academy, whereas I gets a handsome salary to teach mathematics at the same place.

explanation: The subject 'I' takes the base verb, so 'I gets' must be 'I get'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: You have spoilt / the little chance you / had at succeeding.
explanation: 'Chance' takes 'of' + gerund or 'to' + infinitive, so 'had at succeeding' should be 'had of succeeding'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: This is the best novel / I have read, / in a very long time.
explanation: The superlative 'the best' with the present perfect 'I have read' and the time phrase 'in a very long time' is idiomatically correct.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: Sam and Teena / had wondering / what to do this weekend.
explanation: 'Had wondering' is not a valid verb form; it should be 'were wondering' or 'had been wondering'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: She often goes for a walk / with her dog / in the night.

explanation: The fixed prepositional phrase is 'at night', not 'in the night', for habitual actions.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: He will be / waiting for me when / I reaches his home.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The residents of Rameswaram / about the 1940s were quite / orthodox, but were also / tolerant of other communities.
explanation: A decade takes 'in', so 'about the 1940s' should be 'in the 1940s'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Although experts are worried / that retail inflation is rising / at a steep rate, / the crisis will soon blow away.

explanation: The correct idiom for a crisis subsiding is 'blow over', not 'blow away'.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
sentence: I am / cleaning the sofa / when she called me.

prompt: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

prompt: Read the sentence given below and identify if there is an error in it. The error can be in any segment of the sentence which are marked A, B, C, and D. Select option D if there is 'No error'. (A) Ritika angrily / (B) spoke to Kartik / (C) after the meeting / (D) No error.

sentence: There has been / an increase of the number / of road / accidents recently.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. An eucalyptus tree in my backyard acts as a landmark for many to reach my house.
options: acts as a landmark for many
explanation: 'Eucalyptus' begins with the consonant 'yu' sound, so it takes 'a', not 'an'.

prompt: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the
sentence: underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. The children were merry than usual on Sunday.
explanation: 'Than' signals the comparative degree, and two-syllable adjectives ending in -y take -ier: 'merrier'.

prompt: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the
sentence: underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Poverty is the urgent concern in India today.
explanation: 'The' before the adjective indicates the superlative degree, and 'urgent' forms it with 'most': 'the most urgent concern'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He sings good / among all the / contestants in / the singing competition.
explanation: 'Sings' is an action verb and needs the adverb 'well', not the adjective 'good'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I hope that / yesterday's lunch / at Rahul's place / was at your liking.
explanation: The idiomatic phrase is 'to your liking', so 'was at your liking' should be 'was to your liking'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: Stephan, however, contrived / to put away / his departure / for eighteen months.
explanation: 'Put away' means to store; postponing something requires the phrasal verb 'put off', so it should be 'to put off his departure'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My sister Mona / never drinks coffee; / she prefer tea / in the morning.
explanation: The singular subject 'she' needs the singular verb 'prefers' in the simple present.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My mother said / that the thief / Ramesh will learnt / his lesson soon.
explanation: After the modal 'will', the base form of the verb is required: 'will learn', not 'will learnt'.

prompt: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the
sentence: underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. It is easiest to stay calm than to protest.
explanation: 'Than' calls for the comparative degree, so the superlative 'easiest' must become 'easier'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The dancer / performed weird / but the music was / highly enchanting.
explanation: The action verb 'performed' must be modified by the adverb 'weirdly', not the adjective 'weird'.

prompt: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the
sentence: underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. The house seemed much far than she expected.
explanation: 'Than' requires the comparative of 'far' for physical distance, which is 'farther'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He was constantly / gazing on the / crime scene to / find some clues.
explanation: One gazes 'at' something; 'gazing on' is the wrong preposition here.

prompt: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the
sentence: underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Mary is the quieter student of the class.
explanation: Comparison with a whole group ('of the class') requires the superlative 'quietest' after 'the'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: A good lawyer / always looks in the / case before he / attends court.
explanation: 'Look into' means to examine or investigate, so 'looks in the case' should be 'looks into the case'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. My sister is allergic with peanuts, so be cautious when preparing her meal.
explanation: The adjective 'allergic' is always followed by 'to', not 'with'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Dr. Oppenheimer is the exceptional movie of all the movies in recent times.
explanation: 'Of all the movies' compares one item with an entire group, so the superlative 'the most exceptional movie' is needed.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. When I was studying Economics in Delhi University, Ritu was senior than me.
explanation: Latin-origin comparatives ending in -ior, such as 'senior', take 'to' and the objective pronoun: 'senior to me'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She is studying / the medicine / at university / to become a doctor.
explanation: 'Medicine' as a field of study is used in a general sense and takes no article; it should be 'studying medicine'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: He told / his senior, "I / will sung a song / at the party tonight."
explanation: After the modal 'will', the base form of the verb is required: 'will sing a song', not 'will sung'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. John searched thoroughly but could not find his coat nowhere in the house.
explanation: 'Could not' is already negative, so 'nowhere' creates a double negative; it must be 'anywhere in the house'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: It has been / noticed that / across all his faults, / he is admired.
explanation: 'Across' is wrong here; the concessive sense requires 'despite/in spite of all his faults'.

prompt: The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.
sentence: If I was a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country.
explanation: An unreal/improbable condition in the second conditional takes 'were' for all subjects: 'If I were a king'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: His artwork is / more intricate / than any artist / in the gallery.
explanation: In a comparative the subject must be excluded from the group, and like must be compared with like: 'than that of any other artist'.

prompt: The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.
sentence: His aunt who lives at America brought a lot of gifts for him and his sister.
explanation: With countries and large places the preposition 'in' is used, not 'at': 'who lives in America'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Rose painted the most beautifullest picture ever at the art class today!
explanation: 'Most beautifullest' is a double superlative; only 'the most beautiful' is correct.

prompt: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the
sentence: underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Wolfia is the tiny plant in the world.
explanation: 'In the world' signals a superlative comparison, so the superlative form 'tiniest' is required.

prompt: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the
sentence: underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. The new almirah is big than this one.
explanation: 'Than' requires the comparative degree, and short adjectives form it with -er: 'bigger than this one'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I have been / looking by my / cream sweater for / a few weeks now.
explanation: The verb 'look' in the sense of searching takes 'for': 'looking for my cream sweater'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: This boy performed / extremely good / in the / dance competition.
explanation: The action verb 'performed' needs an adverb, so 'extremely good' must be 'extremely well'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: My sister performed / brilliant / in the competition / yesterday.
explanation: The adjective 'brilliant' cannot modify the verb 'performed'; the adverb 'brilliantly' is required.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: They worked / very hardly / on their project / for several weeks.
explanation: 'Hardly' means 'scarcely'; the intended sense of diligent effort needs 'very hard'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She received / an award / for her work / in a engineering field.
explanation: 'Engineering' begins with a vowel sound, so the article must be 'an engineering field'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: How can someone / walk this farthest / just for / peace of mind?
explanation: No superlative is warranted here; the correct expression of distance is 'walk this far'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Please hang with for two minutes while I finish cleaning the utensils.
explanation: The idiom meaning 'wait' is 'hang on', not 'hang with'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in the usage of indefinite articles.
sentence: We have invited / our friends / for a / dinner.
explanation: Names of meals take no article when used generally, so it should be 'for dinner'.

prompt: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the
sentence: underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Yesterday was the worse day of my life.
explanation: 'The' plus 'of my life' requires the superlative 'worst', not the comparative 'worse'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. He bought strange vintage car on auction from the customs department.
explanation: The singular countable noun needs an indefinite article: 'a strange vintage car'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She oftenly goes / shopping with / her friends / on Saturdays.
explanation: 'Oftenly' is not a word; the adverb of frequency is simply 'often' — 'She often goes'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: I still / do not understand / why he did not / reply my email.
explanation: 'Reply' is intransitive here and needs the preposition 'to': 'reply to my email'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in phrasal verb.
sentence: Gita got onto / the book / she was reading / this morning.
explanation: 'Got onto' is wrong for resuming/returning to reading; the correct phrasal verb is 'got back to (the book)'.

prompt: Which of the following sentences contains an error in the use of a phrasal verb?
options: Can you please take care for my belongings for some time?
While visiting the library, I came across an interesting book.
Let's call off the picnic as there is a possibility of heavy rain.
It is wise to put up with one's quarrelsome neighbours.
explanation: The fixed phrasal verb is 'take care of', not 'take care for'.

prompt: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the
sentence: underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Which flower do you like best?
explanation: The superlative degree here requires the definite article: 'Which flower do you like the best?'

prompt: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the
sentence: underlined part are given as options. Choose the correct alternative. She is late than we expected.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The farm cattle is grazing in the field when the tiger attacked.
explanation: 'Cattle' is a plural noun and the past-time clause ('when the tiger attacked') requires past continuous: 'were grazing'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Nagamani, a brave student, lodged a F.I.R. against the criminal.
explanation: 'F.I.R.' begins with the vowel sound /e/, so it takes 'an F.I.R.', not 'a F.I.R.'

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The dog / eager wagged / its tail when / it saw its owner.
explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'wagged': 'eagerly wagged', not the adjective 'eager'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. My son, who is a cricketer too, is a M.A. from Delhi University.
explanation: 'M.A.' starts with the vowel sound /e/, so the correct article is 'an M.A.'

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Please bring two bananas and the piece of cake from the market.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: I regret / in notify that / the model you want/ is out of stock.
explanation: 'Regret' is followed by the infinitive here: 'I regret to notify that', not 'in notify'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: She speaks / so soft that / hardly anyone / can hear her.
explanation: The manner of the action verb 'speaks' needs an adverb: 'so softly that'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.
sentence: That question is / much difficult / but this one is / very easy.
explanation: 'Much' cannot directly qualify a positive adjective; it should be 'very difficult' (or 'much too difficult').

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The 100-year-old banyan was blown off in the storm last night.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: While she / was watched / the movie, / her phone rang.
explanation: The clause needs the active past continuous 'was watching'; the passive 'was watched' is wrong with the object 'the movie'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: They were / interested / on / learning new languages.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Sarah / will singing / at the concert / on Saturday.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Most probably, / he come / to office / next Tuesday.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I have never seen so beautiful a landscape than this one.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The car which I bought last year was cheap than my bike.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Much of the beauty and glory of life have disappeared.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. A fox and an hyena were spotted in the animal reserve.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. Ms. Malathi is old much to join a college now.
explanation: The intensifier must precede the adjective in the 'too + adjective + to + verb' pattern, so 'old much' should be 'too old'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: How long / have you / been learn / English now?
explanation: The present perfect continuous requires 'have been + V-ing', so 'been learn' must be 'been learning'.

prompt: Which of the following sentences contains an error in the use of a phrasal verb?

The old lady broke down when she heard her son lost his job.
Make over the bed daily. It is a good habit.
Try your level best before you decide to give up.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The society / of the / our place / is good.
explanation: An article cannot be used together with a possessive adjective, so 'of the our place' should be 'of our place'.

sentence: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. This is one of best movies I have ever seen.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: We / enjoyed lunch / he gave / us.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

of the new policy on exports.

prompt: The sentence below is split into four segments labelled (A), (B), (C), and (D). One segment contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment with the error.

prompt: The sentence below is split into four segments labelled (A), (B), (C), and (D). One segment contains a grammatical error. Identify the segment with the error.
sentence: It was highly careless about the manager to have approved ten lakh rupees for that unverified project.

prompt: The sentence below is divided into four parts labelled a, b, c, and d. One part contains a grammatical error. Identify the part with the error. The remarkable rise in foreign investments have strengthened the fiscal position of emerging economies.

prompt: A sentence is divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.
sentence: The child yearned over the distant hills and dreamed of adventures beyond the valley.
explanation: 'Yearn' takes the preposition 'for', so it should be 'The child yearned for the distant hills'.

prompt: The sentence below is divided into four parts labelled a, b, c, and d. One part contains a grammatical error. Identify the part with the error.
sentence: She has been working tirelessly to improve the standard of the education in rural areas.
explanation: Abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article, so 'of the education' should be 'of education'.

prompt: A sentence is divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error.

options: It was quite unkind about the
explanation: Adjectives of behaviour in the 'It was + adjective + of + person' pattern take 'of', so it should be 'unkind of the senior manager'.

will exist among the two families

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given

options: shall be a rule rather than a exception

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. Ishwarchand Vidyasagar use the ancient text to suggestion that widows could remarry.
options: used the ancient texts to suggest
use the ancient texts for suggestion

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. Let us not neglect important aspects of life although pursue momentary pleasures.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. Some agitating miners allegation that there is no emergency measures inside the mines.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. He made a desperate but also partial successful effort to change the ghastly topic.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. His school was 7 km away from his house. I wondered how he covered so long distance daily on foot.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. We must endeavour to increase women's access for education also employment.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. Knowing the particular things that motivate each person help you add power to their motivation.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. The big farmers with deepest tubewells still have water, but many others face a water crisis.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given

options: have been looking for a better job
have looked for a better job

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. The female ostrich guards the nest at night and the male guard it in the day.
explanation: The singular subject 'the male' needs 'guards', and 'during the day' is the correct idiomatic phrase.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. The Head has been so busy to go through these files and resolve the matter.
options: too so busy to go through

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. We had never seen so strong blizzard. The wind speed was 130 km per hour .
explanation: With a singular countable noun, the structure is 'such a strong blizzard' (or 'so strong a blizzard').

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. When we went to the cinema yesterday, the film had already start.
explanation: Past perfect requires 'had + V3', so 'had already started' is correct for the earlier of two past actions.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. Each dancer performed very well that it was difficult to judge who the best was.
explanation: 'So + adverb + that' is the correct correlative structure; 'such' cannot modify the adverb 'well'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. If you join this job now, it proves to be good in the long run.

it will prove to be good

have a friend whom parents live

options: seen him for I last left
see him since I last left
seen him since I last left

sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. Applications are to be sent to the Principal before 30th May.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given
sentence: If no substitution is required, select No improvement. She read that novel since she got up in the morning.

explanation: 'Crux' means the most important or central point of a matter.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: Mrs. Lakshmi’s purchases add around to ₹2,650.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

explanation: 'A piece of cake' idiomatically means something very easy to do.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

explanation: After the modal 'may', both verbs must be parallel bare infinitives: 'may manage ... and help in reducing'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: Well, I prefer eating at home from eating out.
explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to' (not 'than' or 'from') when comparing two things.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: He has grown into a beautiful youth.
explanation: 'Beautiful' is used for females; a male youth is described as 'handsome', and 'grow into' is the correct phrasal verb.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: Dhruv’s anger blazed of uncontrollably.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb is 'blaze up', meaning to flare out suddenly.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: One of my best friends are here.
explanation: 'One of + plural noun' takes a singular verb, so 'One of my best friends is here'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.
sentence: The company do not broke the law at any time.
explanation: With the singular subject 'company', the correct form is 'does not break', keeping the base verb after 'does'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: The new chief is gifted at the power of eloquence.
explanation: The fixed collocation is 'gifted with' when describing a talent someone possesses; 'gifted at' is incorrect here.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: There is no way I can swallow the ghastly medicine.
explanation: 'Ghastly' means dreadful or horrible, so 'horrible' is the closest substitute; the other options carry the opposite, positive sense.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.
sentence: Rohit is write to them three times.
explanation: 'Three times' indicates a repeated action completed up to now, so the present perfect 'has written' is required.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.
sentence: There was some drawing-pins in my desk.
explanation: The plural subject 'drawing-pins' after 'there' needs a plural verb, and the present tense fits the context: 'There are some'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: It will take two hours to walk across the forest.
explanation: Movement within a three-dimensional space such as a forest takes 'through', not 'across' (used for surfaces or from side to side).

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.
sentence: There was a noise that was wake me up.
explanation: The relative clause needs a simple past finite verb agreeing with 'that' (the noise): 'a noise that woke me up'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: The meeting closed with a vote of thanks.
explanation: A meeting formally ends, so 'concluded with a vote of thanks' is the idiomatic collocation.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: The skunk had a conspicuous spinal stripe.
explanation: 'Conspicuous' means easily seen, which matches 'noticeable'; 'obscure' and 'faint' are antonyms.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.
sentence: Play cards is not allowed here
explanation: A verb used as the subject of a sentence must be a gerund, so 'Playing cards is not allowed here'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: Do not later about the street.
explanation: The intended verb is 'loiter' (to hang about aimlessly), and it idiomatically takes 'around'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: Mahima is as smarter as Shilpi.
explanation: The 'as ... as' construction of equality requires the positive degree, so 'as smart as' is correct.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: The dictator ordered the traitor were jailed.
explanation: After 'order', the object is followed by an infinitive, giving 'ordered the traitor to be jailed'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: The painting look good in this room.
explanation: The singular subject 'The painting' needs the singular verb 'looks'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: I like played cricket after school.
explanation: 'Like' expressing a habitual preference is followed by a gerund, so 'I like playing cricket'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: Vihaan is clumsy at dancing.
explanation: The idiom 'all thumbs' means clumsy or awkward, matching the sense of the original segment.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: We feel warm on the subject
explanation: The idiomatic expression for having strong feelings about something is 'feel warmly about'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: There is no place on the bench.
explanation: For available space, English uses the uncountable noun 'room', so 'There is no room on the bench'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: Rahul had strong pain in his stomach.
explanation: Pain collocates with 'severe', not 'strong'; the other adjectives do not combine with 'pain'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: I will require a quiet room to work at.
explanation: One works 'in' a room, since a room is an enclosed space; 'work at' takes a place of employment or a task.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: It was her who first saw the criminal.
explanation: After 'It was', the pronoun functions as a complement of the subject and must be in the nominative case: 'It was she who...'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: Please take many as you want.
explanation: 'Take' with the uncountable/indefinite quantity here needs the correlative 'as much as': 'Please take as much as you want.'

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: Once bitten, thrice shy.
explanation: The fixed proverb is 'Once bitten, twice shy', so 'thrice' must be replaced by 'twice'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: He is almost quiet well.
explanation: 'Quiet' (silent) is wrong here; the intensifier 'quite' is needed: 'He is quite well.' 'Almost' is also redundant with 'quite'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: I was in Oman around two months.
explanation: A period of duration takes 'for': 'I was in Oman for two months.'

prompt: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
sentence: Sarita speaks French best.
explanation: With no comparison implied, the simple adverb 'well' modifies 'speaks'; the superlative 'best' needs a basis of comparison.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’
sentence: The forecast predicts that there will be little rain in the month of July.
explanation: 'Rain' is uncountable, so 'little rain' is correct; 'many/few rain' are wrong and 'must be' changes the meaning.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: Everybody who know him agree that he rarely loses his temper.
explanation: 'Everybody' is singular, so both the relative-clause verb and the main verb take -s: 'who knows him agrees that'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: He decided not to take to heart the loss that he had incurred in business.
explanation: 'Decided not to take to heart' is the correct negative infinitive with the fixed idiom 'take to heart', so no change is needed.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: India have a many all-rounders to match the talent and dedication of Kapil Dev.
explanation: 'Have a many' is ungrammatical; 'India' is singular and 'all-rounders' is countable, so 'has few all-rounders' is correct.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: Every year the family goes for a pilgrim to the temple at Tirupathi.
explanation: The idiomatic expression is 'go on a pilgrimage'; 'pilgrim' is the person, not the journey.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: Suman performed at the festival well yesterday.
explanation: Adverb order is manner–place–time, giving 'performed well at the festival yesterday'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: She will have to go to another school when she moves from here, has she ?
explanation: The statement is positive and uses 'will have to', so the tag must be the negative of the auxiliary 'will': 'won't she?'

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: Have taken permission , Shivam went horse riding.
explanation: A completed prior action in a participial phrase requires the perfect participle 'Having taken permission'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ’No substitution required’. When challenged, the man had no answer for his actions.
explanation: 'When challenged' is a correct reduced passive clause (when he was challenged), so no substitution is needed.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: The mare hurt its hooves when running to the forest.
explanation: Movement to the inside of a place requires 'into', not 'to': 'when running into the forest'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: The police was accused to tamper with the evidence.
explanation: 'Accuse' takes the fixed pattern 'accused of + gerund': 'accused of tampering with the evidence.'

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: The young man lifts weights at the gym when he pulled a muscle.
explanation: An ongoing past action interrupted by another past action takes the past continuous: 'was lifting weights when he pulled a muscle'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: I am certain Ashok has finished his work by tomorrow.
explanation: 'By tomorrow' marks completion at a future point, which requires the future perfect 'will have finished'.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

explanation: A simultaneous accompanying action is expressed by the present participle: 'fell down yesterday, narrowly missing my car.'

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: I cannot tell you now whether I will be able to come or not.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

hasn’t stopped us we would reach

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

prompt: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.
sentence: The committee worked up the matter for two hours but could not reach any consensus.
